name: Arms
for: Leveling in a group or beside a healer, with one slow two-hander.
summary: One slow two-hander for group leveling: Improved Overpower and Improved Charge by 18, Anger Management at 22, Sweeping Strikes at 30, Bloodthrill turning Rend into frequent Overpowers from 31, and Mortal Strike at 40. Alone, the Protection build lives longer.
notes: Improved Rend (10 to 12) makes Rend 35% stronger and Deflection (13 and 14) adds 2% parry. Improved Overpower (15 and 16) gives Overpower 50% more crit chance; until Bloodthrill it lights up after a dodge, for 5 Rage. Improved Charge (17 and 18) adds 6 Rage to every Charge, and Improved Tactical Mastery (19 to 21) opens Anger Management at 22: 1 Rage every 3 seconds in combat, and Rage lost 30% more slowly between pulls.

Deep Wounds (23, 24 and 29) bleeds the target for 60% of your weapon’s average damage over 12 sec after each crit. Spearing Strike (25) deals 75% weapon damage, and 75% more to Giants, Dragonkin and mounted targets, for 15 Rage every 20 sec. Two-Handed Weapon Specialization (26 to 28) adds 6% damage.

Sweeping Strikes (30) makes your next 5 swings hit a second mob, and since November 10 a swing that hits no second target keeps its charge. Bloodthrill (31 and 32): keep Rend on the mob and every main-hand hit has a 20% chance to allow an Overpower, which cannot be dodged. Improved Slam (35 and 36) takes Slam’s cooldown from 15 to 10 seconds and stops it delaying your swing: six Slams a minute instead of four. Weaponmaster fills 33, 34 and 37 to 39, and Mortal Strike comes at 40.

Then Cruelty (41 to 45), Unbridled Wrath (46 to 50) and Enrage (51 to 55): every hit you take has a 30% chance to start Enrage, so it is up most of the time while questing. Reckless Swings (56) gives up to 20 Rage over your next four swings. Improved Execute (57 and 58), a point of Impale (59, 10% more crit damage on your abilities) and Piercing Howl (60) finish it.
Mobalytics’ guide skips Improved Tactical Mastery and Anger Management for three more points of Deflection: 5% parry against a steadier Rage income.
At 60 it is 5 points from the Arms PvE build: Deflection, Improved Charge and Piercing Howl become Improved Heroic Strike, a second point of Impale and Improved Bloodrage.

sources.name: Icy Veins Arms warrior leveling guide

name: Fury
for: Warriors with two good one-handers who want the dual-wield playstyle; level as Arms or Protection until you have them.
summary: Dual-wield build that kills fast and heals itself: Enrage from 20, Death Wish at 30, Flurry at 35, Bloodthirst at 40 and Gore Drinker at 44. You need two good one-handers, and Berserker Stance makes you take 10% more damage.
notes: Cruelty (10 to 14) and Unbridled Wrath (15 to 19) work with any weapon. Enrage (20 to 24) has a 30% chance to start on every hit you take, so while questing its 10% Physical damage is up most of the time. Reckless Swings (25) gives up to 20 Rage over your next four swings every 15 seconds.
Furious Precision (26 to 28) and Dual Wield Specialization (29 and 31 to 34) only work with two weapons: until you have a second one-hander, level as Arms. Death Wish (30) opens Bloodthirst (40).
Flurry (35 to 37) makes three swings 30% faster after a crit; at 25% crit about 58% of your swings are faster. Improved Whirlwind (38 and 39) makes Whirlwind a single-target button too.

Blood Craze (41 to 43) opens Gore Drinker (44 and 45): every Bloodthirst, Enrage, Bloodrage or Berserker Rage makes your next three attacks heal 1% of your health each, so 3% per Bloodthirst every 6 seconds. That is what cuts your eating.

Icy Veins’ guide puts the three Furious Precision points right after Unbridled Wrath, from level 20 when you can dual-wield, and Dual Wield Specialization before Death Wish: it suits a warrior who has two good one-handers at 20.
Wowhead’s guide takes Blood Craze and Gore Drinker by 32 and Furious Precision after Bloodthirst: healing from 32 for less off-hand hit until 45.

Improved Berserker Rage (46 and 47), Improved Execute (48 and 49) and an Arms dip finish it: Improved Heroic Strike (50 to 52), Deflection (53 and 54), Improved Charge (55 and 56), Improved Tactical Mastery (57 to 59) and Anger Management (60), which needs it. At 60 it is 11 points from the Fury PvE build.

sources.name: Icy Veins Fury warrior leveling guide

name: Protection
for: Solo questing and grinding with a one-hander and a shield, and tanking the dungeons on the way.
summary: The solo warrior’s build: Revenge hits 60% harder from 17, blocks, dodges and parries pay your Rage, Thunder Clap is cheap from 24, Charge works in Defensive Stance from 25 and Shield Slam lands at 40. You pull two or three mobs and live; a single mob dies more slowly than with Arms.
notes: Shield Specialization (10 to 14) adds 5% block and 5 Rage on every block, so Shield Block pays for itself. Improved Revenge (15 to 17) makes Revenge, learned at 14, hit 60% harder: it costs 5 Rage and follows every block, dodge or parry. Improved Bloodrage (18 and 19) adds 50% to Bloodrage’s Rage.

Master of Defense (20 and 21) adds 5 Rage on every dodge or parry with a shield on. Improved Thunder Clap (22 to 24) takes 6 Rage off Thunder Clap: pull two or three mobs, Thunder Clap them and fight them together. Vanguard (25) lets you Charge without leaving Defensive Stance. Last Stand (26) and Concussion Blow (30, a 5 sec stun) are your emergency buttons.

Anticipation (27 to 29, 34 and 41) adds 20 Defense at five points. Focused Rage (31 to 33) takes 3 Rage off every offensive ability, Bastion (35 to 39) adds 10% to all your damage while you hold a shield, and Shield Slam (40) hits for 421 to 439 plus your Block Value.

From 42: Cruelty (42 to 46, 5% crit), Unbridled Wrath (47 to 51, a 60% chance at 1 more Rage per hit) and Enrage (52 to 56), which stays up because every hit you take can start it, then Reckless Swings (57). Defiance (58 to 60) adds 20% threat in Defensive Stance for the dungeons at 60.
Icy Veins’ and Mobalytics’ guides put three points in Improved Sunder Armor instead of Anticipation: Sunder Armor 3 Rage cheaper, for tanking dungeons, against 12 Defense by 29.

Since November 13 stuns have diminishing returns on creatures again: a second Concussion Blow on the same mob soon after the first is shorter. At 60 it is 5 points from the Protection tank build: Improved Bloodrage, two points of Improved Thunder Clap and Vanguard become Deflection and Improved Shield Wall.

sources.name: Icy Veins Protection warrior leveling guide

name: Arms
for: Raids from December 9 with a two-hander, where your group has no Fury slot to fill.
summary: Mortal Strike, Slam and a stream of Overpowers with one two-hander: Bloodthrill turns Rend into Overpower procs, Improved Slam makes Slam a 10-second cooldown that no longer delays your swing, and Fury adds Cruelty, Enrage and Reckless Swings.
notes: Keep Rend up: Bloodthrill gives each main-hand attack a 20% chance to allow Overpower. With a 3.6-speed weapon plus Mortal Strike and Slam that is about one Overpower every 8 seconds, each for 5 Rage, impossible to dodge and with 50% more crit chance from Improved Overpower.
Improved Slam takes Slam from a 15- to a 10-second cooldown and stops it delaying your swing: six Slams a minute instead of four, all free of swing time.

Reckless Swings gives up to 20 Rage every 15 seconds (5 on each of your next four swings within 8 seconds), up to four times what Anger Management gives, and a point of Improved Bloodrage adds 5 Rage to every Bloodrage. Spearing Strike hits for 150% weapon damage against Dragonkin and Giants, Onyxia included, and 75% against anything else.

name: Fury
for: Raids from December 9 with two one-handers: the warrior’s main raid damage build.
summary: Bloodthirst and Whirlwind with two one-handers: Flurry keeps your swings fast after crits, Improved Whirlwind adds 30% to the closest target every 8 seconds, and the Arms points bring Improved Heroic Strike, Improved Overpower, Anger Management, Deep Wounds and Impale.
notes: With 30% crit about two thirds of your swings get Flurry’s 30% speed, and Bloodthirst and Whirlwind crits refresh it on top.

Improved Whirlwind means a Whirlwind every 8 seconds instead of 10, with 30% more damage to the closest target: about 60% more Whirlwind damage on one boss. A point of Improved Bloodrage adds 5 Rage to every Bloodrage.
Dual Wield Specialization adds 25% off-hand damage and 50% more off-hand Rage, and Furious Precision 10% off-hand hit. Queueing Heroic Strike no longer raises your off-hand hit chance in Forever.
Improved Overpower gives Overpower 50% more crit chance: swap to Battle Stance for it after a dodge, keeping up to 25 Rage through the swap with Improved Tactical Mastery.
Since November 13 a Windfury Totem triggers from every melee ability, but only from its main-hand strike: Bloodthirst and Whirlwind’s main-hand hit can trigger it, Whirlwind’s off-hand hit cannot.
Paladins no longer have Salvation, so hold Death Wish (20% more Physical damage for 30 seconds, 5% more damage taken) until the tank has a lead.
Icy Veins’ build takes all five points of Enrage instead of Improved Execute; its guide names this build’s split for raids where Enrage starts too rarely.

name: Protection
for: Main tank in raids from December 9: the most threat and Defense for five- and ten-player groups.
summary: Shield Slam, Revenge and Thunder Clap from Defensive Stance, which now adds 80% threat before Defiance’s 20%. Shield Specialization, Master of Defense and Focused Rage keep Rage steady, and Anticipation adds 20 Defense.
notes: Shield Block costs 10 Rage and blocks up to two attacks; with Shield Specialization each block returns 5 Rage, so press it on cooldown for mitigation and Revenge at no cost.

Focused Rage takes 3 Rage off every attack: Revenge costs 2, Shield Slam 17 and Sunder Armor 12. One point of Improved Thunder Clap takes 2 more Rage off every Thunder Clap; Charge only works out of combat, so Vanguard is left out.
Deflection (42 to 44) adds 3% parry, and every parry opens Revenge. Icy Veins and Wowhead take it instead of Improved Sunder Armor, since a raid tank gets its Rage from the hits it takes.

Enrage stays up while you tank, since every hit you take has a 30% chance to start it: 10% more Physical damage, so more threat. Reckless Swings gives up to 20 Rage over your next four swings every 15 seconds.
Since November 13 stuns have diminishing returns on creatures again, so Concussion Blow on the same add twice in a row lasts less the second time.
Icy Veins’ build takes Lingering Rage and Vanguard instead of Unbridled Wrath, Reckless Swings, Improved Thunder Clap and Focused Rage’s third point, and two more points of Deflection.
Improved Shield Wall makes Shield Wall a 4-minute cooldown, so it is ready every pull. For five-player dungeons the Protection leveling build at 60 fits better.

name: Arms
for: Battlegrounds and world PvP with a two-hander: Mortal Strike’s healing cut.
summary: Mortal Strike’s 50% healing reduction with two-handed burst: Bloodthrill and Improved Overpower make Overpower a frequent crit, Improved Hamstring and Piercing Howl keep targets close, and Fury adds Cruelty, Enrage and Blood Craze.
notes: Open with Charge (21 Rage with Improved Charge), then Rend, Hamstring and Mortal Strike. Keep Rend up for Bloodthrill’s Overpowers and Mortal Strike on whoever is being healed.

Improved Hamstring gives each Hamstring a 15% chance to root for 5 seconds; proc roots now have diminishing returns, so do not count on chaining them. Piercing Howl slows everyone within 10 yards by 50%.
Improved Tactical Mastery lets you keep 25 Rage through a stance change: Battle for Charge and Overpower, Berserker for Intercept, Pummel and Berserker Rage, Defensive for Disarm.
Deflection adds 2% parry. For shorter crowd control, move Enrage into Iron Will in Protection: 15% shorter stuns and fears.

Omnivore’s Mobalytics PvP guide takes Booming Voice instead of Unbridled Wrath, since its 25% Rage cut reaches Piercing Howl, and five points of Deflection and Spearing Strike instead of Blood Craze and Improved Charge.

name: Fury
for: PvP with two one-handers: mobility and self-healing, no healing cut.
summary: Dual-wield pressure that keeps moving and heals itself: Improved Berserker Rage breaks snares, Bloodthirst keeps 10% movement speed up, Improved Intercept stuns every 20 seconds and Gore Drinker heals after every Bloodthirst. It has no healing reduction.
notes: Improved Berserker Rage makes Berserker Rage give 10 Rage and remove all movement-impairing effects, every 30 seconds; since November 13 it also breaks Sap. Bloodthirst every 6 seconds keeps its 10% movement speed running.

Gore Drinker: Bloodthirst, Enrage, Bloodrage, Berserker Rage and Death Wish each make your next three attacks heal 1% of your health, 3% per Bloodthirst alone. Blood Craze heals 3% more after a crit lands on you.
Death Wish gives 30 seconds of fear immunity and 20% more Physical damage for 5% more damage taken; Berserker Rage covers fear the rest of the time.
Without Mortal Strike a well-healed target can outlast you, so pick targets your team can burst or that fight without a healer.

name: Protection
for: Flag carriers and node defenders: a shield, long cooldowns and control.
summary: A shield build for carrying flags and holding nodes: Shield Wall every 4 minutes, Last Stand, 15% shorter stuns and fears from Iron Will, and control from Concussion Blow, Improved Shield Bash, Improved Disarm and Piercing Howl.
notes: Stay in Defensive Stance: Vanguard lets you Charge there, Thunder Clap makes up to 4 enemies attack 20% slower, and Revenge follows every block, dodge or parry.
Improved Shield Bash adds a 3-second silence to the interrupt, Concussion Blow stuns for 5 seconds, and Improved Disarm brings Disarm down to 40 seconds; shapeshifted druids cannot be disarmed.
Shield Slam has a 50% chance to dispel a magic effect from the target, such as a shield or a buff.
It deals less damage than the Arms and Fury builds: it wins by lasting and by controlling the fight.

name: Retribution
for: Solo questing with a two-hander: the paladin’s fastest leveling build.
summary: Two-hander build that turns Judgement into mana: Sanctified Judgement by 17, Pursuit of Justice at 20, Seal of Command at 22, Vengeance at 30 and Unsealed Wrath at 40. Its Judgements refund the mana its seals cost, and it runs 15% faster between fights.
notes: Deflection (10 to 14) adds 5% parry: fewer hits taken while you fight alone. Sanctified Judgement (15 to 17) refunds 60% of your seal’s cost on every Judgement, and Judgement no longer uses up the seal: with Improved Judgement (18 and 19) you judge every 8 sec, so over a 30-sec seal the refunds come to more than twice its cost, while each Judgement costs 6% of base mana.

Pursuit of Justice (20 and 21) adds 15% to your speed, mounted too; it does not stack with other speed effects. Seal of Command comes at 22, Conviction (23 to 25) adds 6% crit and Sacred Arbiter (26) 20% Holy Strike damage. Two-Handed Weapon Specialization (27 to 29) adds 6% Holy and Physical damage, and Vengeance (30 to 32) stacks up to 15% more damage after crits.

Repentance (33) incapacitates a humanoid for up to 6 sec, and Judgement of Command deals double damage to stunned or incapacitated targets: open with Hammer of Justice or Repentance. A point of Vindication (34) opens Champion of the Light (35 to 39), which turns 60% of your Intellect into spell damage, and Unsealed Wrath lands at 40.

Judgement is a ranged attack since November 11: it uses your ranged hit chance and triggers no melee procs. Since November 13 Judgement of Command is a melee attack again and triggers on-hit effects; your other Judgements stay ranged. Hit is one stat for attacks and spells in Forever, so Precision and hit gear cover both.
Blizzard’s note of November 11 calls the capstone “Unsealed Fury”; the game names it Unsealed Wrath. Since that day its stored seals no longer echo from Windfury Totem attacks.

From 41: Divine Strength (41 to 45, 10% Strength), Improved Seals (46 to 50) for 15% more seal and Judgement damage, Divine Intellect (51 to 55, 10% Intellect, more spell damage through Champion of the Light), Precision (56 to 58) for 3% hit, and Vindication’s last two ranks (59 and 60).
For group leveling, Benediction instead makes seals, Judgement and Holy Strike 10% cheaper.
At 60 it is 7 points from the Retribution PvE build: Deflection and Pursuit of Justice become Benediction and Holy Conduit.

sources.name: Icy Veins Retribution paladin leveling guide

name: Protection
for: Paladins who want to tank dungeons while leveling: Pursuit of Justice first, then Protection.
summary: Shield tank for dungeon groups that runs 15% faster from 21: twelve Retribution points for Pursuit of Justice, then Protection from 22, Shield Specialization (32 and 33), Holy Shield at 42 and Shieldsworn at 52. Solo it kills more slowly than Retribution, but it is the sturdiest way to level.
notes: Benediction (10 to 14) makes seals, Judgement and Holy Strike 10% cheaper, Sanctified Judgement (15 to 17) refunds 60% of your seal’s cost on every Judgement and Improved Judgement (18 and 19) takes 2 sec off Judgement’s cooldown. Pursuit of Justice (20 and 21) adds 15% to your speed, mounted too; it does not stack with other speed effects.

Righteous Fury comes at 10, so you can tank your first dungeon: 33% more threat, and 90% more from Holy damage. Redoubt (22 to 26) is the entry to Shield Specialization (32 and 33): every block restores 4% of your maximum mana, at most once every 3 sec. Precision (27 to 29) adds 3% hit and Sacred Duty (30 and 31) takes 60 sec off Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Templar’s Bulwark.

Templar’s Bulwark (34) absorbs damage equal to your maximum health for 8 sec, Swift Judgement (37) is a second Judgement on its own 1-min cooldown, and Improved Righteous Fury (38 to 40) cuts the damage you take by 9%. Toughness (35, 36, 41, 51 and 53) adds 10% to the armor from your items.

Holy Shield at 42, Reckoning (43 to 46 and 50) for extra attacks after blocks, Iron Creed (47 to 49) and Shieldsworn at 52: Holy Strike every 6 sec, each one firing Holy Shield and Shield Specialization. Anticipation (54 to 58) adds 20 Defense and Conviction (59 and 60) 4% crit.
Since November 13 stuns have diminishing returns on creatures again, so Hammer of Justice on the same mob twice is shorter the second time.
At 60 it is 7 points from the Protection tank build: Benediction and Pursuit of Justice become Deflection, Stoicism and a third point of Conviction.

sources.name: Icy Veins Protection paladin leveling guide
Mobalytics Protection paladin leveling guide (Axphyxiate Gaming)

name: Holy
for: Paladins who heal dungeons on the way up. Solo it kills slowly; Method’s guide levels as Retribution and turns Holy later.
summary: Healer build for dungeon groups: Illumination by 24, Oath of Light at 25, Holy Shock at 30 and Light’s Vigil at 40. Alone it kills slowly, so heal dungeons or level as Retribution.
notes: Spiritual Focus (10 to 14) keeps Flash of Light and Holy Light casting through hits 70% of the time, and Healing Light (15 to 17) adds 12% to Holy Light, Flash of Light and Holy Shock.

Reverence (18 and 19) keeps 30% of your mana regeneration while casting and opens Illumination (20 to 24): every critical heal refunds half its base cost. Oath of Light (25) goes on your tank, Infusion of Light (26 and 27) takes a second off your next Holy Light after a crit, and Divine Favor (28) guarantees one.
Holy Shock at 30, Boundless Light (31 and 32) for 30% more Holy Shock crit on allies without your Oath, Holy Power (35 to 39) and Light’s Vigil at 40.
After 40 come Benediction (41 to 45), Conviction (46 to 48) for 6% crit and Divine Intellect (49 to 53), then Sanctified Judgement, Pursuit of Justice, Guardian’s Favor and Sacred Duty.

Icy Veins’ guide spends the first twelve points in Retribution for Pursuit of Justice by level 21, then turns Holy and reaches Light’s Vigil twelve levels later than this build. Wowhead’s guide offers both starts: Reverence early for mana in dungeons, as here, or Pursuit of Justice first for travel.
It ends on the Holy PvE build point for point, so there is nothing to respec.

sources.name: Icy Veins Holy paladin leveling guide

name: Holy
for: Raid and dungeon healers from December 9: Holy Light, Flash of Light and Holy Shock with the most mana back from crits.
summary: Oath of Light on the tank, Holy Shock on everyone else, and Infusion of Light turns each Shock or Flash of Light crit into a 1.5-sec Holy Light. Conviction from Retribution adds the 6% crit that Illumination, Holy Power and Boundless Light all build on.
notes: Oath of Light adds up to 400 to Holy Light, 115 to Flash of Light and 230 to Holy Shock on one ally for 5 min. Boundless Light gives Holy Shock 30% more crit on everyone else, which keeps Infusion of Light and Illumination going.

Conviction is the best buy outside Holy: through Illumination, 6% more crits refund about 3% of the mana you spend, about what Divine Intellect adds to your pool over a five-minute fight, and the crits heal more on top. Divine Intellect is in too, for the pool.
Light’s Vigil and the Holy Shock that spends it cost 1,665 mana together for 684 to 724 healing on each member of a party, so save it for damage that hits most of the party.
Pursuit of Justice adds 15% speed. Guardian’s Favor puts Blessing of Protection on a 3-min cooldown and makes Blessing of Freedom last 16 sec; Sacred Duty takes 30 sec off Divine Shield.

name: Protection
for: Paladin tanks for dungeons and raids: Holy Shield, Shieldsworn and Consecration on packs.
summary: Holy damage under Righteous Fury does the threat, Shieldsworn’s 6-sec Holy Strike fires Holy Shield and Shield Specialization, and blocks pay for your mana. Deflection and Conviction from Retribution add 5% parry and 6% crit.
notes: Shieldsworn takes 4 sec off Holy Strike and makes it strike with your shield: each one deals Holy Shield’s 221 Holy damage (rank 4, from 60) and restores 4% of your maximum mana without spending a charge or waiting out the 3-sec limit, and lets you block spells for 6 sec.

Iron Creed’s 6% damage reduction lasts 6 sec, as long as Holy Strike’s cooldown, so it never drops if you press Holy Strike on cooldown; with Improved Righteous Fury’s 9% you take about 14% less damage.

Sanctified Judgement returns 120 mana on every Judgement with Seal of Fury (60% of 200), every 8 sec with Improved Judgement. With Shield Specialization that covers Consecration on packs, so Divine Intellect and Reverence stay out.
Templar’s Bulwark is your cooldown: Divine Protection stops you attacking, Divine Shield halves your damage and threat, and all three share Forbearance.

Icy Veins’ tank build takes Benediction, Pursuit of Justice and Sacred Arbiter instead of Deflection, Stoicism and two points of Toughness: instant spells 10% cheaper, 15% speed and 20% more Holy Strike damage, for 5% less parry. Wowhead’s standard build also takes Pursuit of Justice and Sacred Arbiter rather than the last two points of Toughness.

name: Retribution
for: Raids from December 9 with a two-hander and Seal of Command.
summary: Two-handed Seal of Command with Unsealed Wrath, Vengeance and Improved Seals. Precision’s 3% hit and Holy Conduit’s cheaper Hammer of Wrath fill the last points.
notes: Judgement no longer uses up your seal: judge Seal of Command every 8 sec and keep it. Sanctified Judgement returns 126 mana each time (60% of 210).

Since November 13 Judgement of Command is a melee attack again: it uses your melee hit and triggers your on-hit effects, a Windfury Totem’s included. Your other Judgements stay ranged attacks, as they are since November 11.
Vengeance stacks five times for 15% more Physical and Holy damage, and Two-Handed Weapon Specialization adds 6% more and cuts your threat by 20%, which matters now that Salvation is gone.

Precision is worth more than further Holy points while you are below the hit cap: 3% hit for three points. Divine Intellect, its entry fee, feeds Champion of the Light, which turns 60% of your Intellect into spell damage and makes Hammer of Wrath instant.

Holy Conduit makes Hammer of Wrath, Consecration and Exorcism 40% cheaper. Vindication lowers the target’s attack power by 204; one paladin per raid is enough, so a second one can move those points into Pursuit of Justice and Unyielding Faith, as the Icy Veins and Wowhead builds do by default.

name: Holy
for: PvP healers: Holy Shock, Blessing of Freedom and Protection on short cooldowns.
summary: 31 points in Holy with Divine Precision, plus Templar’s Bulwark, Sacred Duty, Improved Righteous Fury and a 45-sec Hammer of Justice from Protection: a healer built to survive focus fire in battlegrounds.
notes: Keep Righteous Fury on: threat means nothing against players, and Improved Righteous Fury cuts all damage you take by 9%. After a resurrection The Quick and the Dead makes it free.

Divine Shield, Divine Protection, Blessing of Protection and Templar’s Bulwark all apply Forbearance, so plan one a minute. Sacred Duty takes 1 min off the cooldowns of Divine Shield, Divine Protection and Templar’s Bulwark and 10 sec off Forbearance.

Guardian’s Favor puts Blessing of Protection on a 3-min cooldown and makes Blessing of Freedom last 16 sec on its 20-sec cooldown. Improved Hammer of Justice puts your 6-sec stun on a 45-sec cooldown, and Divine Precision cuts silences by 20%.
Templar’s Bulwark became a Magic effect on November 2, so priests, shamans and Felhunters can strip it.

name: Retribution
for: PvP burst around a stun and a doubled Judgement of Command.
summary: Burst around Judgement of Command, which doubles against stunned or incapacitated targets: Hammer of Justice every 45 sec, Swift Judgement for a second doubled Judgement, and Templar’s Bulwark and Improved Righteous Fury from Protection to stay in the fight.
notes: Stun, then Judgement, Swift Judgement and Holy Strike: at 60 each Judgement of Command on a stunned target deals 339 to 373 before talents and spell damage. Repentance (up to 6 sec on a humanoid) sets up the same Judgement, but the damage wakes the target.
Unsealed Wrath in PvP: swing under Seal of Justice to store copies, then switch to Seal of Command. Your next hit rolls each copy for its 2-sec stun, and a stunned target takes a doubled Judgement.
Unyielding Faith cuts fears and disorients by 30%, Pursuit of Justice adds 15% speed, and Champion of the Light makes Hammer of Wrath an instant finisher below 20% health.
Against warlocks, swap Unyielding Faith for Turn Evil: Turn Undead then works on their demon, with a 0.5-sec cast and a 20-sec cooldown.

name: Protection
for: Flag carriers and node defenders: blocks, stun and charm resistance, Blessing of Freedom.
summary: The toughest of the three PvP builds, made to carry flags and hold nodes rather than to kill: Stoicism, Improved Righteous Fury, Iron Creed and a 6-sec Holy Strike that keeps spell blocking up, with Pursuit of Justice and Unyielding Faith from Retribution.
notes: Shieldsworn’s Holy Strike every 6 sec keeps Iron Creed’s 6% damage reduction and spell blocking running, and each one restores 4% of your maximum mana.
Stoicism cuts stuns and charms by 20% and Unyielding Faith fears and disorients by 30%. Guardian’s Favor makes Blessing of Freedom last 16 sec on its 20-sec cooldown.
Reckoning stores an extra attack after every critical hit you take, up to four, and your next swing spends them all.
Improved Hammer of Justice puts your stun on a 45-sec cooldown to stop a chaser, and Templar’s Bulwark comes every 4 min with Sacred Duty.

name: Beast Mastery
for: Solo questing, and the default for any hunter: the pet tanks while you shoot.
summary: Ranged speed first: Deadly Aspects from level 10, a pet that comes back fast, Pathfinding at 20, two hawks at 25, Intimidation at 30 and Bestial Wrath at 40. Auto Shot costs no mana, so the points that feed it save drinking.
notes: Deadly Aspects (10 to 14) gives Auto Shot a 10% chance to make your shots 30% faster for 12 sec while Aspect of the Hawk is on. Auto Shot costs nothing, so this pays in every fight. Focused Fire (15 and 16) adds 2% to everything you and the pet deal.

Improved Revive Pet (17 and 18) takes 6 sec off Revive Pet’s cast and 40% off its mana, and the pet comes back with 30% more health. One point of Endurance Training (19) adds 3% to the pet’s Health and Armor and opens the next row; since November 10 a pet has 115% of its normal health. Pathfinding (20 and 21) makes Aspect of the Cheetah 6% faster, and running is a large part of leveling.

Unleashed Fury (22 to 24 and 26) adds 12% to the damage of your pet and hawks, Summon Hawk (25) sends a hawk for 18 sec, two at a time, and Ferocity (27, 28 and 31 to 33) gives both 10% more crit. Since November 10 the hawks hit about 80% harder and cost 11% of base mana. Summon Hawk shares Arcane Shot’s cooldown: keep two hawks out and use Aimed Shot as your other shot.

Intimidation (30) stuns the target for 3 sec on the pet’s next hit. Bestial Discipline (34 and 39) keeps 50% of your mana regeneration running while you shoot, Frenzy (35 to 38) gives the pet an 80% chance at 30% attack speed for 8 sec after it crits, and Bestial Wrath (40) adds 50% to the pet’s damage for 18 sec.

From 41 the points go to Marksmanship: Lethal Attacks (41 to 45, 5% crit), Careful Aim (46 to 50, Attack Power equal to your Intellect), Rapid Killing (51 and 52: 20% on your next shot after a kill, Rapid Fire 2 min sooner), Efficiency (53 to 57, shots and stings 15% cheaper), Trueshot Aura (58) and two points of Mortal Shots.

At 60 it is 7 points from the Beast Mastery PvE build: Improved Revive Pet, Pathfinding, Rapid Killing’s second point and Mortal Shots move to Endurance Training, Unleashed Fury, Frenzy and Improved Stings.

sources.name: Icy Veins Beast Mastery hunter leveling guide

name: Marksmanship
for: Players who want to kill with their own shots and keep the pet as a tank; slower to start than Beast Mastery.
summary: Shot-first build: Lethal Attacks and Efficiency first, Rapid Killing at 20, Mortal Shots (28 to 32), Rapid Recuperation (33 and 34) and Sniper Shot at 40. You kill with your own shots and drink less after 34, but an untalented pet loses mobs to you more often than a Beast Mastery pet.
notes: Lethal Attacks (10 to 14) adds 5% crit, and Efficiency (15 to 19) takes 15% off every shot and sting, which matters more than damage while your mana bar is small.

Rapid Killing (20 and 21) buffs your next shot by 20% after every kill, and Rapid Recuperation (33 and 34) turns that into mana: open each pull with Serpent Sting and a shot that uses up Rapid Killing, and all of your mana regeneration keeps running while you shoot for 15 sec.

Careful Aim (22 to 24, 26 and 27) turns Intellect into Attack Power and Trueshot Aura comes at 25. Mortal Shots (28 to 32) adds 30% to the crit damage of your ranged abilities, Ranged Weapon Specialization (35 to 39) adds 5% ranged damage and Sniper Shot comes at 40.

From 41: Improved Stings (41 to 43, 20% more Serpent Sting damage), Barrage (44 to 46, 15% more Multi-Shot, Aimed Shot and Volley damage), Deadly Aspects (47 to 51), Improved Tracking (52 to 56) and Survivalist (57 to 60, 8% more health).

Icy Veins and Wowhead put the points after 40 into Beast Mastery instead of Improved Tracking and Survivalist (Focused Fire, Unleashed Fury, and Summon Hawk in Icy Veins’ build), and Wowhead’s leveling build leaves out Sniper Shot.
At 60 it is 1 point from the Marksmanship PvE build: the fourth point of Survivalist becomes Lone Wolf once you leave the pet behind.

sources.name: Icy Veins Marksmanship hunter leveling guide

name: Survival
for: Players who enjoy melee: Raptor Strike, Mongoose Bite and Strider Kick beside the pet, with more eating than a ranged hunter.
summary: Melee hunter build: Improved Tracking first, Deterrence at 20, Predator’s Edge by 29, Strider Kick at 30 and Lacerating Strikes at 40. You fight beside your pet and take more hits, so you eat more often than a ranged hunter.
notes: Improved Tracking (10 to 14) adds 5% damage against the creature type you track, so keep Track Beasts or Track Humanoids on for what you are killing.

Savage Strikes (15 and 16), Survivalist (17 to 19), Deterrence (20) and Surefooted (21 to 23, 3% hit) make melee survivable. Predator’s Edge (25 to 29) adds 30% crit damage to your melee abilities and 50% off-hand damage.

Strider Kick (30) and Lacerate from the trainer join Raptor Strike and Mongoose Bite. Resourcefulness (31 and 32) cuts melee and trap costs by 60%, Expose Prey (33 and 34) lets hits on a target with Hunter’s Mark enable Mongoose Bite, Lightning Reflexes fills 35 to 39 and Lacerating Strikes lands at 40.

Levels 41 to 60 take Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim, Deadly Aspects (fight in Aspect of the Beast), Focused Fire, Survivalist’s Discipline (an Immolation Trap at your feet every 18 sec) and a second point of Clever Traps.

Icy Veins’ guide takes Lethal Attacks first and reaches Lacerating Strikes five levels later; Wowhead’s plays Beast Mastery to 32 and respecs, because Survival’s melee needs Strider Kick and Expose Prey.
At 60 it is 2 points from the Survival PvE build: Focused Fire becomes Lone Wolf and a fourth point of Survivalist.

sources.name: Icy Veins Survival hunter leveling guide

name: Marksmanship
for: Raids from December 9, without a pet: the most damage for the least mana.
summary: No pet, 20% more damage, and almost every other point spent on mana or on free damage, because at 60 you run out of mana long before you run out of cooldowns. Trueshot Aura gives the raid’s hunters 100 Ranged Attack Power.
notes: Lone Wolf adds 20% to everything you deal while no pet is out, so it wins whenever your pet deals less than a fifth of your own damage. Measure yours on a target dummy with and without the pet before you commit; pets inherit your crit chance and have had 115% health since November 10.

Aimed Shot on every cooldown plus Serpent Sting costs 4,100 mana a minute. Efficiency (15% cheaper), Rapid Recuperation (half your regeneration while you shoot) and Improved Stings (+20% to Serpent Sting, your most mana-efficient attack) earn their points; Improved Arcane Shot, for your least efficient shot, does not.
Auto Shot costs nothing and is about half your damage: Deadly Aspects (about 13% more Auto Shots), Ranged Weapon Specialization and Improved Tracking (+5% against the type you track) feed it.

Mortal Shots takes five points instead of Surefooted and two of Survivalist: it adds 30% to the crit damage of your ranged abilities, about 7.5% more damage from them at 25% crit, where Surefooted’s 3% hit needed eight points. Three points of Survivalist add 6% Health.

name: Beast Mastery
for: Raids where the pet survives the fight: two hawks and a pet carry the damage while your mana lasts longest.
summary: Your pet and two hawks carry a large share of the damage while Bestial Discipline and Efficiency stretch your mana, and Bestial Wrath is the burst every 2 minutes, with Rapid Fire every other time.
notes: Unleashed Fury and Ferocity buff the hawks as well as the pet, and pets inherit your crit chance, so Lethal Attacks also feeds Frenzy.
Summon Hawk shares Arcane Shot’s cooldown and Improved Arcane Shot does not shorten it, so keep two hawks out, use Aimed Shot as your other shot and save Arcane Shot for moving.
Deadly Aspects comes first: Auto Shot costs nothing, and its 10% proc means about 13% more Auto Shots.
Only one Trueshot Aura counts in a raid. If a Marksmanship hunter brings it, move that point and Rapid Killing into two more ranks of Endurance Training.
Bring a Wolf if your raid has none: Furious Howl gives 83 melee Attack Power to everyone within 15 yards of it.

Icy Veins’ build takes Mortal Shots and Rapid Killing’s second point instead of Efficiency and Trueshot Aura, and Improved Revive Pet instead of two points of Endurance Training: 30% more crit damage on your shots, for fights short enough that you never run out of mana.
Wowhead’s build rates Improved Tracking higher than Mortal Shots, as a bonus on all the damage you deal to the tracked type, and keeps Trueshot Aura.

sources.name: Icy Veins Beast Mastery hunter talents

name: Survival
for: Raid groups that want a melee hunter: no pet, Raptor Strike and Mongoose Bite, traps for extra damage.
summary: A melee hunter without a pet: Lone Wolf, Predator’s Edge and Lightning Reflexes behind Raptor Strike, Mongoose Bite and Strider Kick, with an Immolation Trap at your feet every 18 seconds.
notes: Fight in Aspect of the Beast (110 melee Attack Power at 60): Hunter’s Mark and Aspect of the Hawk only raise Ranged Attack Power, and so does the Trueshot Aura of another hunter. Keep Hunter’s Mark up anyway, because Expose Prey needs it.
Lacerating Strikes always overwrites, so each Mongoose Bite replaces the bleed instead of stacking it: with a Bite every 8 sec it adds about 15% to Bite’s damage.
Clever Traps and Survivalist’s Discipline turn traps into damage: Fire traps scale with Attack Power, all traps share one cooldown, and the talent cuts it from 30 to 18 sec.
Resourcefulness cuts melee and trap costs by 60%, so the build needs no Efficiency, and Deadly Aspects procs from your melee swings in Aspect of the Beast.
A slow two-hander hits hardest, since Raptor Strike, Mongoose Bite and Strider Kick use weapon damage; Predator’s Edge’s 50% off-hand bonus makes dual-wielding an option once you have hit to spare.

Icy Veins’ and Wowhead’s melee builds leave Lacerating Strikes out and go down Beast Mastery to Summon Hawk instead; Wowhead keeps Lacerating Strikes for a hunter who weaves shots and melee with a two-hander.

name: Marksmanship
for: Battlegrounds and world PvP from range: Scatter Shot, traps and burst.
summary: Burst and control from range: Scatter Shot, Improved Concussive Shot and traps keep enemies off you while Aimed Shot, Arcane Shot and Sniper Shot do the damage.
notes: Scatter Shot needs 21 Marksmanship points, so only this spec has it next to its capstone. Scatter, step back and drop a Freezing Trap where the target will run at you.
Improved Arcane Shot (an instant every 4.5 sec while you kite), Mortal Shots and Barrage put the burst into shots you can land; Sniper Shot opens from 45 yards.
Hawk Eye adds 6 yards of range, Improved Concussive Shot gives Concussive Shot a 20% chance to stun for 3 sec, and Improved Stings brings Viper Sting down to a 9 sec cooldown to drain healers.

Improved Wing Clip gives Wing Clip a 20% chance to root a melee attacker for 5 sec (shorter if it lands again soon, since 2 November). Two points of Survivalist, Surefooted (30% shorter snares) and Deterrence keep you alive, and Improved Tracking adds 5% against players with Track Humanoids on.
Keep the pet: a Bird of Prey’s Mine! disarms for 3 sec, a Crocolisk’s Dismember cuts healing by 25% and a Bat’s Sonic Blast slows casting by 30%.

Icy Veins’ PvP and world build and Feor’s Mobalytics PvP guide take Rapid Killing, Rapid Recuperation and Ranged Weapon Specialization instead of Improved Arcane Shot and Improved Concussive Shot: mana for battlegrounds, where kills come often. Improved Concussive Shot’s stun suits duels.

sources.name: Icy Veins Marksmanship hunter talents (PvP / World / Leveling build)

name: Beast Mastery
for: PvP where the pet can reach its target: pressure that keeps working while you kite.
summary: Pet pressure that keeps working while you kite: Intimidation, Bestial Wrath and two hawks, a pet built to stay alive, and Deterrence for you.
notes: Your pet and hawks keep dealing damage while you move, which matters now that Auto Shot needs you to stand still for half a second.
Intimidation stuns for 3 sec on the pet’s next hit, and Bestial Wrath makes the pet unstoppable for 18 sec.
Endurance Training, Improved Revive Pet (a 4 sec revive at 45% Health) and Spirit Bond (1% Health every 5 sec for you and the pet) keep the pet fighting; Bestial Discipline keeps your mana going.

Lethal Attacks raises your crit and the pet’s, which inherits it. Improved Tracking, Survivalist, Deterrence and Surefooted come from Survival: Surefooted 3/3 gives 3% hit and 30% shorter snares, so 2% hit from gear stops your shots missing players.
It has no Scatter Shot, and its damage drops while the pet is controlled or dead, so pick fights the pet can reach.
Icy Veins’ PvP and world build takes Entrapment, Clever Traps and Survival Tactics instead of Survivalist and Lethal Attacks: traps that root everything they catch for 5 sec, with 10% more hit.

sources.name: Icy Veins Beast Mastery hunter talents (PvP / World / Leveling build)

name: Survival
for: PvP at every range: roots, traps and melee where other hunters are weakest.
summary: A melee hunter who still shoots: no dead zone, roots from Improved Wing Clip and Counterattack, a trap every 18 seconds and Deterrence every 3 minutes.
notes: You fight at every range: shoot while enemies come to you, then Raptor Strike, Mongoose Bite and Strider Kick in melee, where a ranged hunter is weakest. Strider Kick also works while you are disarmed.
Survivalist’s Discipline cuts trap and Deterrence cooldowns by 40%, and Clever Traps makes Freezing and Frost Trap effects last 30% longer.

Improved Wing Clip (a 20% chance to root for 5 sec) and Counterattack (a 5 sec root after you parry) hold targets in place, and Strider Kick gives 30% speed for 3 sec to catch up. Roots from procs now share diminishing returns.
It has no Scatter Shot and must reach its target: against casters who kite, open with a trap and Wing Clip rather than chasing.

name: Combat
for: Solo questing with any one-handed weapons: the rogue’s default leveling build.
summary: Sinister Strike into Eviscerate with any one-handers. Damage before defense: cheaper Sinister Strike and Eviscerate first, Riposte at 20, Blade Flurry at 30 with Dual Wield Specialization right after, Flash of Steel from 35 and Adrenaline Rush at 40.
notes: Efficient Strikes (10 and 11) drops Sinister Strike’s cost by 5 Energy, Coup de Grace (12 to 14) adds 20% to Eviscerate, and Precision (15, 16 and 21) adds 3% hit so fewer strikes miss.

Deflection (17 to 19) adds 6% parry and opens Riposte (20): 150% weapon damage and a 6 sec disarm after you parry, for 10 Energy. Precision’s third point waits so that Riposte comes at 20. Composure (22 and 23) makes Poised, a passive you learn at 18, take 20 Energy off the first ability of each pull, and one point of Endurance (24) puts Evasion and Sprint 30% sooner; these fill the 15 points the fourth row needs.

Flawless Execution (25) takes 15 Energy off Eviscerate, Aggression (26 to 28) adds 15% to Sinister Strike and Eviscerate, and Weapon Expertise (29 and 33) takes 2% off the chance to be dodged or parried.

Blade Flurry (30) gives 20% attack speed and hits a second mob for 15 sec, every 2 min: pull two mobs when it is ready. Dual Wield Specialization (31 and 32) adds 50% to your off-hand’s damage, the most damage per point in the tree, and Hack and Slash (34 and 43 to 46) gives swords and axes a 5% chance at an extra attack, daggers and fists 5% crit, maces 15% armor ignored.

Flash of Steel (35 to 39) makes Shank, trained at 24, return 15 more Energy and come back 2 sec sooner, so keep it on cooldown. Adrenaline Rush lands at 40. Remorseless Attacks (41 and 42) gives your next Sinister Strike a 40% increased critical strike chance for 20 sec after each kill. From 47: Malice (47 to 51, 5% crit), Ruthlessness (52 to 54), Improved Slice and Dice (55, 56 and 59), Lethality (57 and 58) and Cold Blood (60).

Mobalytics’ Combat guides take Remorseless Attacks first instead: the first strike on each mob crits more from level 10, and Riposte, Blade Flurry and Adrenaline Rush each come two levels later. It suits a player who chains easy kills.
At 60 it is 3 points from the Combat PvE build: Riposte and Remorseless Attacks become a second point of Endurance and two points of Vigor.

name: Subtlety
for: Rogues who open from Stealth with daggers: Ambush and Shank combo points, Death Mark at 40.
summary: Open each pull from Stealth with Premeditation and Ambush, then build with Hemorrhage from 30 and Shank with Boot Knife from 35. It needs a dagger in the main hand and does most of its damage in the opener, so it kills slower than Combat in long fights.
notes: Opportunity (10-14) adds 20% to Backstab, Garrote and Ambush. Dirty Deeds (15-16) takes 20 Energy off Cheap Shot and Garrote and lets you Garrote from the front. Camouflage (17), then Improved Ambush (18-19 and 24, +45% crit) for Ambush, trained at 18.

Premeditation at 20 and Initiative (21-23) make Premeditation and Ambush a four-point opener. Ghostly Strike at 25 deals 180% weapon damage with a dagger, adds 15% dodge and lets your next Ambush or Garrote skip Stealth; with Dirty Deeds that is a Garrote from the front every 20 sec.

Serrated Blades (26-28) and Elusiveness (29 and 31) lead to Hemorrhage at 30: 145% weapon damage with a dagger for 35 Energy, from any side. Heightened Senses (32-33) and Preparation (34), a second Vanish and Evasion when a pull goes wrong, open the next row.

Boot Knife (35-39) makes every Shank add 2 combo points, and Death Mark lands at 40. From 41: Efficient Strikes, Coup de Grace and Precision from Combat, then Malice, Ruthlessness, Improved Slice and Dice, Lethality and Blood Splatter.
At 60 this is the Subtlety PvE build, so there is nothing to respec.

name: Assassination
for: Rogues who will raid Assassination with daggers: slower before Mutilate at 40, two points from the raid build at 60.
summary: A crit and poison build that strikes with Sinister Strike until Mutilate arrives at 40, with Venom from 30 and Seal Fate from 35. It levels slower than Combat before 40 and Mutilate needs daggers, but it ends 2 points from the Assassination PvE build.
notes: Remorseless Attacks first (10-11): after each kill, your next Sinister Strike, Backstab, Ambush or Mutilate has 40% more crit chance. Malice (12-14 and 18-19) adds 5% crit, and Ruthlessness (15-17) gives finishers a 60% chance to add a combo point.
Lethality (20-21), Vigor (22-23) and Blood Splatter (24; Garrote lasts 9 sec longer, so open with it) lead to Cold Blood at 25 and Vile Poisons (26-29).

Venom at 30: each Shank, trained at 24, raises your poison damage by 30% and your chance to apply poisons by 20% for 6 sec. Relentless Strikes (31-34 and 38) makes every five-point finisher return 25 Energy once all five ranks are in, Seal Fate (35-37) adds a combo point when a builder crits, and Mutilate lands at 40.

After Mutilate at 40: Coup de Grace, Precision and Puncturing Wounds (Mutilate +15% crit) from Combat, Opportunity (Mutilate +16%), then Lightning Reflexes (44 and 45), Endurance, Improved Sprint and Flawless Execution.
At 60 it is 2 points from the Assassination PvE build: move Remorseless Attacks to Improved Slice and Dice.

name: Combat
for: Raids from December 9 with swords, axes or maces: the rogue’s main raid build.
summary: Sinister Strike and Eviscerate with a sword, axe, mace or fist weapon. Combat does the most sustained damage of the three trees, and Flash of Steel, Dual Wield Specialization and Adrenaline Rush are the reason.
notes: Keep Slice and Dice up (Improved Slice and Dice adds 45%), use Shank on cooldown (40 Energy every 8 sec with Flash of Steel), Sinister Strike to five points, then Eviscerate: 20 Energy with Flawless Execution, and Coup de Grace and Aggression add 20% and 15% to it. Blade Flurry and Adrenaline Rush together.

Hack and Slash follows your weapon: fist weapons gain 5% crit, swords and axes a 5% chance of an extra attack, maces ignore 15% armor. At equal weapon damage they are within about 2% of each other, so take your strongest weapon; with a dagger in the main hand, use the daggers build.

Precision is the only hit talent a rogue has, and Weapon Expertise takes 2% off dodge and parry. Deflection, Endurance and Composure pay for row 4: Endurance puts Evasion and Sprint on a 2 min cooldown, and Composure makes Poised take 20 Energy off the first ability of each pull.

name: Combat daggers
for: Raids with two daggers before you have Mutilate gear: Backstab from Combat.
summary: The same Combat engine with Backstab as the builder: Puncturing Wounds adds 30% crit and a 45% chance of a second combo point, Opportunity adds 20%, and Hack and Slash adds 5% crit with daggers. With a good dagger and the boss’s back to you, it does a few percent more than the Sinister Strike build.
notes: Efficient Strikes only helps Sinister Strike and the third rank of Aggression adds just 5% to Eviscerate, so they make room for Puncturing Wounds and Opportunity; Lightning Reflexes and Improved Sprint fill the early rows.
Priority: Slice and Dice, Shank on cooldown, Backstab to five points, Eviscerate. On fights where you cannot stay behind the target, use the Sinister Strike build.

name: Assassination
for: Raids with two daggers: Mutilate, Seal Fate and poisons.
summary: Mutilate with two daggers: two combo points a press, a third from Seal Fate when it crits, and Relentless Strikes returning 25 Energy on every five-point finisher. Shank on cooldown keeps Venom’s 30% poison bonus up 6 of every 10 seconds, and Flawless Execution from Combat makes Eviscerate cost 20 Energy.
notes: The 16 Combat points carry the build: Precision for hit, Puncturing Wounds for 15% more Mutilate crit and so more Seal Fate points, and Coup de Grace and Flawless Execution for Eviscerate. Four points of Opportunity add 16% to Mutilate and Garrote.
Open with Garrote (Blood Splatter adds 9 sec), keep Slice and Dice and Rupture up (6 sec longer), Shank on cooldown for Venom, Mutilate to four or five points, Eviscerate with the rest.

Improved Poisons and Improved Expose Armor are left out: row 4 needs filler points on the way to Venom and Relentless Strikes, and Vile Poisons’ 20% more poison damage beats a higher chance to apply them; Improved Expose Armor no longer adds to the armor reduction. Take it only if your raid asks you to keep Expose Armor up.

name: Subtlety
for: Raid groups that want Death Mark and Hemorrhage’s bleed bonus; behind Combat for damage.
summary: Hemorrhage and Shank with Boot Knife build the combo points, Ghostly Strike opens a Garrote every 20 sec, and Death Mark at five points stores 60% of your damage for 6 sec (twice that from Garrote and Rupture) and deals it again, up to 1,381 at rank 4, a cap that rises with your Attack Power and crit.
notes: Blood Splatter makes Garrote last 27 sec and Rupture 6 sec longer, Hemorrhage adds 15% to both, and Serrated Blades adds 30% to Rupture and ignores 9% armor.
From Combat: Efficient Strikes (Hemorrhage costs 30 Energy), Precision for hit, and Coup de Grace, which raises Death Mark’s storage rate and damage by 20% as well as Eviscerate.

Priority: Slice and Dice, Rupture, Hemorrhage’s debuff, Shank on cooldown, Ghostly Strike into Garrote (or Ambush from behind if Garrote is still running), Death Mark at five points, Eviscerate with the rest.

name: Subtlety
for: Battlegrounds and world PvP from Stealth: long openers and Death Mark.
summary: The control spec: Premeditation, Initiative and Dirty Deeds turn Cheap Shot into a five-point opener, Preparation gives you a second Vanish, Evasion, Sprint and Blind, and Boot Knife and Death Mark supply the burst.
notes: Premeditation adds 2 points and Cheap Shot 3 with Initiative, for 20 Energy: 60, less 20 from Dirty Deeds and 20 from Poised with Composure. A Sap first uses up Poised, so wait for full Energy (Poised comes back out of combat) before the Cheap Shot. Spend them on Death Mark, rebuild with Shank and Hemorrhage, and Kidney Shot as Cheap Shot ends.

Elusiveness puts Vanish and Blind on a 3 min 30 sec cooldown, Dirty Tricks halves the cost of Sap and Blind, and Heightened Senses makes spells and ranged attacks miss you 4% more often. Master of Deception and Camouflage help you open first.
From Combat: Improved Sprint (Sprint clears snares), Endurance (Evasion and Sprint every 2 min), Improved Kick (2 sec silence), and Precision and Weapon Expertise so your stuns and Kicks land.
Death Mark is a Curse: mages and druids can remove it, and Orcs can Shatter Curse it.

name: Combat
for: PvP with swords or maces: steady damage, Riposte and Blade Flurry.
summary: A duelist for long fights: Riposte disarms for 6 sec, Endurance brings Evasion and Sprint back every 2 min, and Adrenaline Rush with Cold Blood is the burst. Maces suit it best, since Hack and Slash then ignores 15% of the target’s armor.
notes: Improved Gouge from Assassination makes Gouge last 5.5 sec, long enough to start a bandage or reset a fight; Improved Kick silences for 2 sec and Improved Sprint clears snares.
Flash of Steel keeps Energy coming between cooldowns, and Precision and Weapon Expertise make your stuns, Kicks and Gouges land.
It has no Premeditation or Preparation, so its openers are smaller and it has one Vanish; it is at its best once the fight is already on.

name: Assassination
for: PvP burst from Stealth with daggers: Kidney Shot, Cold Blood and Mutilate.
summary: Burst from Stealth: Premeditation and Initiative set up an early Kidney Shot, Improved Kidney Shot adds 10% damage while it lasts, and Mutilate with Seal Fate refills the combo points for Cold Blood and Eviscerate.
notes: Venom and Vile Poisons keep poisons on the target: each Shank adds 20% to your poison application chance for 6 sec, and Vile Poisons gives them a 24% chance to resist dispels. Crippling Poison on one weapon keeps targets from running.
Opportunity adds 20% to Mutilate, Dirty Deeds makes Cheap Shot cost 40 Energy, and Elusiveness, Dirty Tricks and Improved Gouge cover the escapes.

It has no Improved Sprint or Endurance, so snares and kiting classes are its hardest matchups: open on them from Stealth and keep Crippling Poison up. It has no Precision either, so the 5% hit that stops your attacks missing players has to come from gear.

name: Shadow
for: Solo questing with no respec: Shadow from 10, Wand Specialization first, Shadowform at 42.
summary: Mind Blast and Shadow Word: Pain to open, Mind Flay and the wand to finish, with Spirit Tap and Vampiric Embrace cutting your downtime and Shadowform at 42. Every point is one you keep, so it needs no respec.
notes: Wand Specialization (10 and 11) adds 25% to your wand damage: open with spells, finish with the wand and keep your mana. Spirit Tap (12 to 16) doubles your Spirit for 15 sec after each kill and keeps 50% of your regeneration running while you cast: pull the next mob while it lasts. Improved Mind Blast (17 to 21) takes 2.5 sec off Mind Blast’s cooldown, about one more Mind Blast per fight.
Mind Flay (22) slows the target by 50%, and Improved Mind Flay (23 and 24) makes each tick deal 20% more than the one before. Shadow Focus (25, 26, 31, 35 and 36) adds 5% hit with Shadow spells.

Vampiric Embrace (27) heals your party for 20% of your Shadow damage, and a mob that dies with it on also triggers Spirit Tap. Shadow Weaving (28 to 30) builds to 10% more Shadow damage, Devouring Contagion (32 and 33) halves Devouring Plague’s cost and spreads it when the target dies, Silence comes at 34, Darkness (37 to 41) adds 10% Shadow damage and Shadowform lands at 42.

Since November 9 casting Fear Ward no longer ends Shadowform, and since November 11 a Gnome can use Confounding Flash in it. Another path is the Discipline leveling build, with Penance at 30 and Meditation early, then a respec to this build at 40. Leave Wand Specialization out of that respec and Shadowform is yours two levels sooner.

From 43: Twin Disciplines (43 to 47, 5% on instant spells), Mental Strength (48 to 52, 10% Intellect), Meditation (53 to 55), which keeps 50% of your regeneration running while you cast even when Spirit Tap is down, Mental Agility (56 to 58), Inner Focus (59) and a point of Dark Inspiration (60).

At 60 the Shadow PvE build is 8 points away: Wand Specialization, Spirit Tap and the fifth point of Improved Mind Blast move to Improved Shadow Word: Pain, four more points of Dark Inspiration and Shadow Reach.

name: Discipline
for: Priests who heal dungeons on the way, or who want Penance at 30 and a respec to Shadow at 40, the path Method’s guide takes.
summary: Smite, Shadow Word: Pain and the wand to kill, a cheap Power Word: Shield without a cooldown to stay safe, and Penance at 30. It levels slower than Shadow but can heal any dungeon on the way.
notes: Wand Specialization (10 and 11) and Power in Light (12 to 16) first: open with Shadow Word: Pain, and Smite deals 10% more to that target. One point of Holy Precision (17) adds 6% hit to Smite and Holy Fire, which covers same-level mobs.

Meditation (20-22) keeps half your regeneration running while you cast, and Mental Agility (23-25) takes 10% off Smite, Holy Fire and your instants. Improved Power Word: Shield (26 to 28) and Soul Warding (29) make the shield absorb 20% more, cost 15% less and lose its 4 second cooldown.
Penance (30) heals or hits three times in 2 seconds. Spirit Tap (31-35) doubles your Spirit after each kill, and Improved Inner Fire (36-38) adds 45% to Inner Fire’s armor and 12 charges.
Twin Disciplines, Inner Focus and Power Infusion (45) come next, then Renewed Hope (46-50) and Divine Aegis (51-53) for dungeon healing.
Icy Veins’ Discipline leveling guide takes Spirit Tap right after Wand Specialization and Penance later, which drinks less while questing alone.

If you turn Shadow at 40, the respec costs gold at your class trainer; Secondary Talents, the second specialization Blizzard opens at 40, keep this build for dungeons. At 60 the Discipline PvE build is 16 points away: Wand Specialization, Power in Light, Holy Precision, Spirit Tap and Improved Inner Fire move to Improved Renew, Divine Fury, Inspiration, Improved Healing, Holy Binding and a fifth point of Mental Strength.

name: Holy
for: Priests who spend most of their leveling in dungeons as the healer; solo it kills slowly.
summary: Level as a dungeon healer: Divine Fury speeds up Smite and Heal, Holy Nova arrives at 20 and Prayer of Mending at 40. Solo it kills slowly, so mix questing with dungeons.
notes: Improved Renew and two points of Holy Specialization open Divine Fury 5/5 (15-19), which takes 0.5 seconds off Smite, Holy Fire, Heal and Greater Heal.

Holy Nova (20) heals your party and hits every enemy within 10 yards without causing threat. Improved Healing (25-27) takes 15% off Lesser Heal, Heal, Greater Heal and Prayer of Mending, and Holy Binding (28) heals you for half of every Flash Heal you cast on someone else.

Litany of Light (30-31) refunds 10% of a heal’s base cost when it differs from the heal before it. Spiritual Guidance (32-36), Spirit of Redemption and Spiritual Healing lead to Prayer of Mending at 40.
From 43 the points go to Discipline: Twin Disciplines and Mental Strength open Meditation (53-55), then Mental Agility and Inner Focus.

For questing alone, Icy Veins’ Holy leveling guide takes Wand Specialization and Spirit Tap first instead, reaches Meditation before most Holy talents, and takes Prayer of Mending only in the late 50s.
It has the same 51 talents as the Holy PvE build in a leveling order, so at 60 it is 0 points away.

name: Holy
for: Raid healers from December 9: Prayer of Mending, Greater Heal and the most healing per mana.
summary: The priest’s first pick for PvE: Spiritual Healing, Spiritual Guidance and Prayer of Mending give it the most healing of the three specs. Litany of Light refunds mana whenever you alternate heals.
notes: Spiritual Healing adds 10% to every heal and Spiritual Guidance adds 25% of your Spirit as healing power, so Spirit pays twice: once as healing, once as mana through Meditation.
Keep Prayer of Mending bouncing: rank 3 heals 413 each time it triggers and jumps up to five times, and Improved Healing and Mental Agility take 15% and 10% off its 390 mana.
Divine Fury cuts Heal and Greater Heal to 2.5 seconds, and Inspiration gives your tank 25% more armor for 15 seconds after any of your non-periodic crit heals.
The 18 Discipline points buy Meditation (50% of your regeneration while casting), Mental Strength (+10% Intellect), Mental Agility and Inner Focus.

name: Discipline
for: Tank and raid healers who shield: Penance, Power Word: Shield and Power Infusion.
summary: An absorb healer: Soul Warding removes Power Word: Shield’s cooldown, Renewed Hope lets you shield the same player again sooner, and every crit heal leaves a Divine Aegis shield. Penance is the efficient burst heal and Power Infusion your cooldown for another player.
notes: Power Word: Shield never overheals and stops pushback, though Penance heals more per point of mana: Improved Power Word: Shield adds 20% to the absorb (928 becomes about 1,114 at rank 10), Soul Warding takes 15% off the cost and removes the 4 second cooldown, and Mental Agility takes another 10% off.

Renewed Hope gives Flash Heal, Heal, Greater Heal and Penance 10% more crit on a target with Weakened Soul and cuts Weakened Soul by 5 seconds each time, so heal a shielded tank and you can shield it again sooner.
Each non-periodic crit heal leaves a Divine Aegis shield worth 15% of the heal (up to 1,200) and Inspiration’s 25% armor; Holy Specialization adds 5% crit.

Penance at rank 4 heals 425 three times for 385 mana before Improved Healing’s 15% discount: cast it on cooldown. Power Infusion (20% more spell damage and healing for 15 seconds) goes to another healer or your best caster.

name: Shadow
for: Raids from December 9 as Shadow: Shadow Weaving for every warlock and Shadow priest.
summary: Shadowform halves the cost of every Shadow spell and doubles its crit damage bonus, and Shadow Weaving and Darkness add 10% each. Mana is the limit, so most of the other points save it.
notes: A full rotation spends more mana than you regenerate even in Shadowform, so the build buys Devouring Contagion (half-price Devouring Plague), Improved Shadow Word: Pain (24 seconds per cast), Meditation, Mental Agility and Inner Focus.
Shadow Focus 5/5 is the only Shadow hit talent. Improved Mind Flay (each tick 20% stronger than the last) and Shadow Weaving are the best damage per point after Shadowform.
Twin Disciplines adds 5% to Mind Flay, Shadow Word: Pain, Devouring Plague and Shadow Word: Death; of your damage spells it misses only Mind Blast.
Dark Inspiration 5/5 gives you and your party 15% more Spirit after Mind Blast or a full Mind Flay, and Silence is your interrupt.
Improved Mind Blast stops at 4/5: it brings Mind Blast’s cooldown from 8 to 6 sec, which two 3-sec Mind Flays fill exactly, and a fifth point’s 5.5 sec adds no cast.
Where a fight puts steady damage on the raid, Twilight Focus (a 70% chance not to lose casting time when hit) can take Mental Agility’s three points instead.
Early Demise is left out: on a boss Shadow Word: Death rarely kills, so nearly every cast costs you 30% of your health, and the extra crit only applies below 20%.

name: Discipline
for: PvP healers who must survive melee: shields, Penance and shorter stuns.
summary: The hardest priest to kill: shields without a cooldown, Penance and Divine Aegis to heal through focus, and a 2 second Mana Burn for enemy healers. The Holy points add Spell Warding, Blessed Recovery and Holy Binding.
notes: Silent Resolve, Martyrdom and Improved Inner Fire are the defense against melee. From Holy, Spell Warding takes 10% off spell damage and Twilight Focus gives every spell a 70% chance not to lose casting time when you are hit, in Shadowform too since November 11.

Soul Warding removes Power Word: Shield’s cooldown, and Renewed Hope cuts Weakened Soul by 5 seconds for each Flash Heal, Heal, Greater Heal or Penance you land on that player, so you can shield the focused target again sooner.
Improved Mana Burn makes Mana Burn a 2 second cast; rank 5 drains 746 to 788 mana. Use it on healers while your team is safe.

Holy Binding heals you for half of every Flash Heal you cast on a teammate, Blessed Recovery heals back 25% of a melee or ranged crit over 6 seconds, and Power Infusion goes on you when focused or on a teammate for a kill.

name: Shadow
for: PvP damage and control: Silence, Psychic Scream and Blackout.
summary: Damage and control: Silence, Psychic Scream every 26 seconds and Blackout stuns, with Mind Blast and Shadow Word: Death to burst. Shadowform takes 15% off Physical damage but blocks heals, so Power Word: Shield and Vampiric Embrace keep you up.
notes: Shadow Focus 4/5 gives the 4% hit that stops Psychic Scream, Silence and Mind Flay missing players of your level. The fifth rank only matters against higher levels.
Blackout 5/5 gives your Shadow damage spells a 10% chance to stun for 3 seconds and opens Improved Psychic Scream. Shadow Reach lets Silence and Mind Flay reach 24 yards.

One point of Early Demise adds 15% crit to Shadow Word: Death below 20% health, and crits deal double damage in Shadowform. Only cast it when it will kill: a miss no longer hurts you, but a target that survives costs you 30% of your health.

From Discipline: Silent Resolve (15% shorter stuns, fears and silences), Martyrdom (no pushback and 20% interrupt resistance after a melee or ranged crit), Improved Power Word: Shield and Improved Inner Fire (45% more armor, 32 charges).
Since November 9 casting Fear Ward no longer ends Shadowform, so keep Fear Ward up on yourself against warriors and warlocks.

name: Holy
for: PvP healers who out-heal pressure: Holy’s big heals and Spirit of Redemption.
summary: The most healing of the PvP builds: Spiritual Healing, Prayer of Mending and Holy Nova, and Spirit of Redemption gives you 15 seconds of free healing after you die. The Discipline points add Improved Inner Fire, Silent Resolve and Martyrdom.
notes: Prayer of Mending heals whoever takes damage next and jumps up to five times, so recast it on cooldown. Holy Nova is an instant heal on the move, and its damage knocks stealthed enemies within 10 yards out of stealth.

Blessed Recovery heals back 25% of a melee or ranged crit, or of any hit over 30% of your health, over 6 seconds; Spell Warding takes 10% off spell damage, and Inspiration adds 25% armor to anyone you crit-heal.
Holy Binding heals you for half of every Flash Heal you cast on a teammate.
From Discipline: Silent Resolve, Martyrdom, Improved Power Word: Shield, Meditation and Improved Inner Fire.

name: Enhancement
for: Solo questing with a two-hander: the shaman’s default leveling build.
summary: Melee with a two-hander, Rockbiter Weapon to 30 and Windfury Weapon after, with shocks to open and finish. Stormstrike at 25, Flurry by 35 and Rage of the Farseer at 40; most of your damage costs no mana, and you wear mail from 40.
notes: Thundering Strikes first (5% crit with spells and attacks), then Mental Dexterity at 15 to 17: Attack Power equal to 33%, 66% and then 100% of your Intellect. Shamanistic Focus at 20 makes shocks and Lightning Shield 45% cheaper.

Rockbiter Weapon until 30, made 20% stronger by Elemental Weapons (21 to 23), then Windfury Weapon, which Elemental Weapons makes 40% stronger. Since the Shaman changes (listed in Blizzard’s hotfixes of 10 November and live in every region since 12 November) your own Windfury Totem (from 32) works alongside it, so your swings get a chance at both, and since November 13 the totem procs from the main-hand strike of every melee ability.

Stormstrike at 25 (100% weapon damage every 8 sec, and 20% more on your next Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning or Earth Shock) and instant Ghost Wolf at 26 and 27. Improved Stormstrike at 30 and 31 resets Stormstrike whenever you dodge or parry, which is why Anticipation (24, 52 and 53) and Spirit Weapons, the talent that lets you parry, at 32 are in the build.

Flurry fills 28, 29 and 33 to 35. Mental Quickness (36 and 37) turns 30% of your Intellect into spell damage for your shocks and opens Rage of the Farseer at 40: 30% attack speed for 25 sec. Maelstrom Weapon (38, 39 and 41 to 43) takes 20% off your next Lightning Bolt’s cast time and mana for every stack, so five stacks make it instant and free.

Maelstrom Weapon’s ranks only change how often it procs: about 6 times a minute at one point, 10 at five. Its tooltip gives the chance per hit for your weapon’s speed, so a slow two-hander procs more per swing.

Then Tidal Focus (44 to 48) for 5% hit, Mindfulness (49 to 51) for mana while you fight and Toughness (54 to 58) for health. Wear Strength and Attack Power first: on November 6 Blizzard said Strength should always be the Enhancement shaman’s best stat and told leveling shamans to collect it.

Icy Veins’ and Wowhead’s leveling builds leave Rage of the Farseer out and spend those points on Tidal Focus, Mindfulness and other trees instead: that path drinks less and hits softer, and suits a shaman who runs out of mana between pulls.

The level-60 build is 10 points from the Enhancement PvE build: Anticipation, Improved Ghost Wolf and Toughness become Convection, Elemental Devastation, Concussion and a fifth point of Ancestral Knowledge.

name: Elemental
for: Shamans who prefer casting: Lightning Bolt and shocks from range, more drinking than Enhancement.
summary: Lightning Bolt from range, Flame Shock on the move and Earthbind Totem to root whatever reaches you. It kills quickly but drinks more often than Enhancement.
notes: Concussion first (Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning and Earth Shock deal 5% more), then Elemental Alacrity at 15-17 for a 2-second Lightning Bolt, Call of Flame at 18-19 and 21 (Flame Shock lasts 9 seconds longer and hits 15% harder) and Elemental Focus at 20 for free casts. Convection (22 to 24, 29 and 34) then makes shocks and bolts 10% cheaper.

Earthbound at 25 makes Earthbind Totem root nearby enemies for 5 seconds: drop it when a mob reaches you, step back and keep casting. Eye of the Storm at 26-28 gives your bolts a 70% chance to ignore pushback.

Lightning Overload at 30-32 comes before Call of Thunder at 33: its first rank alone adds 5% damage, while Call of Thunder’s 5% crit is worth about 2% until Elemental Fury (35-39) doubles your crit damage bonus. Lightning Mastery follows at 40.

From 41: Tidal Focus (5% hit), Mindfulness, Improved Reincarnation and Water Shield at 51, which returns 2% of your mana when a mob hits you or a spell crits. Elemental Reach (52-53) lets you pull from 36 yards, then Thundering Strikes and Trial by Fire for pulls of two or three.
The level-60 build is 3 points from the Elemental PvE build: Earthbound and Trial by Fire become Elemental Warding.

name: Restoration
for: Shamans who heal dungeons on the way up; solo it kills slowly.
summary: Heal dungeons with Healing Wave and, from 40, Chain Heal and Riptide, and quest with shocks and Lightning Bolt in between. It levels more slowly than the other two specs but needs no respec at 60.
notes: Tidal Focus first (heals 5% cheaper, 5% hit for your shocks), Mindfulness at 15-17 so half your regeneration continues while you cast, and Water Shield at 20: 2% of your mana back when you are hit or a spell crits.
Healing Focus at 21-23 (70% chance to ignore pushback), Mana Tide Totem at 25, Nature’s Swiftness at 30 and Healing Way at 31-33, which adds 25% to Healing Wave.
Purification at 35-39 adds 10% to all your heals, and Riptide comes at 40 with Chain Heal: Chain Heal cast on the Riptide target heals it for 25% more.
Thundering Strikes at 41-45 adds 5% crit to heals and attacks alike. Improved Healing Wave (18-19, 24 and 46-47) makes Healing Wave half a second faster.
It has the same 51 talents as the Restoration PvE build, so it is 0 points away.

name: Restoration
for: Raid and dungeon healers from December 9: Chain Heal and totems.
summary: Riptide on cooldown, Chain Heal starting on the Riptide target, and Healing Wave for the tank. Water Shield, Mindfulness and Mana Tide Totem carry your mana.
notes: Healing Way (25% more Healing Wave) and Purification (10% more healing) are the biggest gains. Riptide no longer heals up front, so cast it before the damage lands.
Thundering Strikes adds 5% crit to your heals, and each crit can return 2% of your mana through Water Shield. Ancestral Healing raises the target’s armor by 25% for 15 seconds after a crit.
If your healing pulls adds onto you, move three points from Restorative Totems into Natural Grace for 15% less threat.

name: Enhancement
for: Raids from December 9 with a two-hander: Stormstrike, Windfury and Maelstrom Weapon.
summary: Stormstrike every 8 seconds, its 20% bonus spent on Earth Shock or an instant Lightning Bolt from Maelstrom Weapon, and Mental Dexterity turning Intellect into Attack Power.
notes: Tidal Focus is your hit talent: its 5% is worth up to about 7% more melee damage against a raid boss, until you reach the cap. Mindfulness adds to Improved Stormstrike’s regeneration so you can keep shocking.

Imbue: Windfury Weapon, made 40% stronger by Elemental Weapons. Since the Shaman changes (listed in Blizzard’s hotfixes of 10 November and live in every region since 12 November) it works together with a Windfury Totem, which since November 13 procs from the main-hand strike of every melee ability, so with one in your group your swings get a chance at both, and Spirit Weapons cuts your threat by 30% while Rockbiter is not on.
Elemental Devastation adds 9% melee crit for 10 seconds after a spell crit. Convection opens it and makes your shocks cheaper still.
Icy Veins’ raid build puts this build’s Tidal Focus and Mindfulness points into Elemental instead, up to Trial by Fire for Fire Nova, and counts on a paladin’s Judgement of Wisdom for mana.

name: Elemental
for: Raids from December 9 as a caster: Lightning Bolt, Chain Lightning and totems.
summary: Lightning Bolt in 2 seconds, Chain Lightning when it hits two or more targets, and Lightning Mastery for burst. Lightning Overload, Call of Thunder and Elemental Fury make every bolt count.
notes: Restoration supplies Tidal Focus (5% hit, worth about 6% damage against a raid boss), Mindfulness and Water Shield, which together keep you casting through a long fight.
Thundering Strikes adds 5% crit, worth about 4% damage with Elemental Fury. Eye of the Storm, Elemental Warding and Elemental Reach keep you casting when the fight comes to you.
For dungeons, move Elemental Warding into Trial by Fire and Earthbound: Fire Nova every 6 seconds, a Magma Totem that lasts 20 seconds longer, and a root for packs that reach you.

name: Enhancement
for: PvP burst that interrupts cannot stop: Stormstrike, Earth Shock and instant Lightning Bolts.
summary: Instant burst that interrupts cannot stop: Stormstrike, Earth Shock on its bonus, Windfury procs and a free Lightning Bolt at five Maelstrom stacks. Instant Ghost Wolf, Toughness, dodge and parry keep you in the fight.
notes: Improved Stormstrike resets Stormstrike whenever you dodge or parry, so Anticipation (6% dodge) and Spirit Weapons (parry) add damage as well as defense.
Tidal Focus’s 5% hit stops your attacks and shocks missing players of your level. Improved Reincarnation adds 4% health and brings Reincarnation back 20 minutes sooner.
Guardian Totems readies Grounding Totem every 13 seconds, and Earth’s Grasp widens Earthbind Totem and toughens Stoneclaw Totem against pets.
Use Windfury Weapon here: its two-attack procs are your burst, and unlike a Windfury Totem it cannot be killed.

name: Restoration
for: PvP healers: Nature’s Swiftness, totems and Chain Heal.
summary: Nature’s Swiftness, Riptide and Healing Wave keep a team alive while Healing Focus protects your casts. Seventeen Enhancement points buy instant Ghost Wolf, Grounding Totem every 13 seconds and 6% dodge.
notes: Riptide is your instant heal on the move (12-second cooldown), and Nature’s Swiftness makes the next Healing Wave instant when someone is about to die.
Ancestral Healing adds 25% armor for 15 seconds after a heal crits, which blunts warriors and rogues, and Water Shield turns their hits into mana.
Thundering Strikes and Ancestral Knowledge open the Enhancement points with 5% crit and 10% Intellect; Guardian Totems and Anticipation lead to Improved Ghost Wolf.

name: Elemental
for: PvP casters: Lightning Bolt and Earth Shock burst with Elemental Mastery.
summary: Shocks every 5 seconds, Earthbind Totem roots and the burst of Lightning Mastery when you get room to cast. Eye of the Storm and Elemental Warding keep you casting under fire.
notes: Reverberation brings your shocks to a 5-second cooldown: Earth Shock to interrupt or finish, Frost Shock to slow, Flame Shock for steady damage. Earthbound roots everything near your Earthbind Totem for 5 seconds.
Burst with Lightning Mastery: Lightning Bolts at 1.5 seconds on one target, Chain Lightning back to back on two or more. Lightning Overload and Elemental Fury make the crits count.

Thundering Strikes adds 5% crit and opens Guardian Totems, whose one point brings Grounding Totem back every 14 seconds. Four points of Tidal Focus give the 4% hit that stops your spells missing players of your level.

name: Frost
for: Solo questing for any mage: freezes and slows keep mobs off you, and you drink the least.
summary: The safest way to level a mage and, with the least drinking, the fastest. Frostbolt slows, Frost Nova and Frostbite freeze, Ice Lance and Shatter punish anything frozen, and from 40 Ice Barrier absorbs damage and adds about 20% Frost damage on every pull.
notes: Frostbolt from range; when the mob arrives, Frost Nova, step back, then Ice Lance (20) and Frostbolt while it is frozen. Damage can break Frost Nova’s freeze, and since November 13 so do Blizzard and damage from procs, so put your biggest hit in first. A frozen target takes 300% more damage from Ice Lance, and Shatter (26-28) adds 50% crit against it. Ice Lance shares its 8 second cooldown with Fire Blast.

Frostbite (15-17) freezes on 15% of your Chill effects and Fingers of Frost (30-31) makes your next two spells count as frozen, so most kills get a shatter without Frost Nova. Frost Channeling (21-23) cuts Frost costs by 15%.

Winter’s Chill (38-39, 100% from 43) stacks on every Frostbolt: finish with Cone of Cold when the mob reaches you, 35% stronger from 46. From 40, cast Ice Barrier before every pull; its cooldown is 30 seconds.

Rank 1 Frostbolt is a one-second cast with Improved Frostbolt and now procs Frostbite and Fingers of Frost at the full rate, so use it to slow a second mob cheaply. Only Blizzard keeps the low-rank penalty.

From 47 the points go to Arcane, for mana. Its first row has nothing a Frost mage casts, so Arcane Resilience (47 to 49, Armor equal to 75% of your Intellect) and two points of Improved Channeling (50 and 51) are the price of the second row. Missile Barrage (52 and 53) gives each Frostbolt a 20% chance to make your next Arcane Missiles cost no mana and channel in half the time, and Arcane Concentration (54 to 58) gives every damage spell a 10% chance to make the next one free. Precision’s third point (59) adds 2% hit and Frost Warding (60) adds 10% to what Ice Barrier absorbs. Icy Veins (November 10) and Wowhead (November 11) leave Missile Barrage out and end on Wand Specialization and Arcane Subtlety instead. It stays here: a Missile Barrage Arcane Missiles fires its five missiles of 209 damage in 2.5 seconds for no mana, about twice what a 457 to 493 Frostbolt deals in that time.
At 60 the Frost PvE build is 4 points away: Frostbite and Frost Warding into Arcane Subtlety and Magic Absorption.

name: Arcane
for: Mages who want the fastest kills and accept more drinking and no freezes.
