summary: Arcane Missiles that damage cannot push back, free Missiles from Missile Barrage and Arcane Wrath to open. It kills quickly but has none of Frost’s freezes and spends more time drinking.
notes: Wand Specialization (10 and 11) adds 25% to your wand, which does most of your damage while your mana pool is small, and Improved Channeling (12-14 and 23-24) ends with Arcane Missiles immune to pushback. Those five points open Missile Barrage (15-16): Fireball and Frostbolt get a 20% chance, Arcane Blast (20) a 40% chance, to make your next Missiles free and twice as fast. Icy Veins (November 4) and Wowhead (November 10) both start with Wand Specialization.

From 25, open with Arcane Wrath (instant with Presence of Mind from 30), cast two or three Arcane Blasts, then Missiles on every proc. Each Blast adds 12% of your Intellect as spell damage for 18 seconds and makes the next one cost 100% more, so stop at two when mana runs low.

Arcane Meditation (26-28) keeps half your mana regeneration going while you cast, and Mage Armor allows another 50%. Arcane Concentration (17-19 and 21-22) makes 10% of your spells free: spend it on a Blast at three or four stacks.

Arcane Power (40) adds 30% damage for 15 seconds for 30% more mana. Accelerant (45-49) takes half a second off Arcane Wrath, and Incineration (50-54) adds 10% crit to Arcane Blast. Improved Fire Blast (57-58) brings Fire Blast back 2 seconds sooner and 15 yards farther, and Arcane Subtlety (59-60) lowers the target’s resistance to all your spells by 15; both guides end on them. Both take Precision earlier and reach Arcane Power later, Icy Veins at level 42 and Wowhead at 55.
At 60 the Arcane PvE build is 7 points away: Wand Specialization, three points of Accelerant and Arcane Resilience into Ignite, Pyroblast and Heating Up.

name: Fire
for: Mages who level in groups and dungeons: big crits, slow to start.
summary: The biggest openers of the three: 41-yard Pyroblasts, Fire Blast on cooldown and Heating Up for fast Pyroblasts. It spends the most mana and has none of Frost’s freezes, so expect more drinking.
notes: Flame Throwing (18-19) adds 6 yards to every Fire spell, so open with a 41-yard Pyroblast (20). Improved Fire Blast (21-22) brings Fire Blast back every 6 seconds and lets it reach 41 yards too. Icy Veins (November 4) levels in Arcane to 29 instead, for Arcane Blast, Arcane Concentration and Missile Barrage, then goes Fire from 30 and reaches Combustion only at level 60: that path suits a mage who wants Arcane Missiles procs early. Wowhead (November 4) starts with Accelerant too, but ends with eighteen Arcane points instead of Impact, Blast Wave and Improved Scorch.
Every Fire Blast adds a Heating Up stack (25), two if it crits. At two stacks Pyroblast is a three-second cast, at three it takes 1.5 seconds.
Impact (15-17) stuns on 10% of your Fire hits, Burning Soul (23-24 and 26) stops 70% of pushback, and Blast Wave (30) dazes everything around you by 50%.
Critical Mass (31-33) and Ignite (27-29 and 34-35) turn your crits into burns and Heating Up stacks; Master of Elements (39 and 41-42) refunds 30% of their base mana cost.
At 60 the Fire PvE build is 9 points away: Impact, Flame Throwing, Burning Soul and Blast Wave into Arcane Concentration, Arcane Subtlety, Arcane Blast and Arcane Meditation.

name: Frost
for: Raids from December 9 as Frost: steady Frostbolts and the least threat.
summary: Frostbolt with Ice Barrier’s 20% Frost damage, Fingers of Frost shatters and Winter’s Chill into Cone of Cold. It is the cheapest mage damage to keep up through a long fight.
notes: Keep Ice Barrier up: 15% more Frost damage for a minute and another 5% while the shield holds. That is about 20% for one global cooldown every 30 to 60 seconds.

Every Frostbolt adds a Winter’s Chill stack. At five, Cone of Cold deals double damage plus 35% of your spell damage, and Improved Cone of Cold adds 35% more, so stand close to the boss when the fight allows it. Arctic Reach makes the cone 20% longer.

On a Fingers of Frost proc, cast Ice Lance, then Frostbolt: both count as hitting a frozen target, so Ice Lance deals 300% more damage and both get Shatter’s 50% crit. It works on bosses that cannot be frozen.

Frost Channeling cuts Frost costs by 15% and Frost threat by 30%, which matters now that Blessing of Salvation is gone. From Arcane, Arcane Subtlety lowers the target’s resistance to all your spells by 15, Missile Barrage gives each Frostbolt a 20% chance at free Missiles and Arcane Concentration makes 10% of your spells free. Frost Warding is left out: it adds no damage. Icy Veins (November 10) and Wowhead (November 4) also leave Missile Barrage out; it stays, because a free Arcane Missiles fires five missiles of 209 damage in 2.5 seconds, about twice a 457 to 493 Frostbolt in that time.

name: Fire
for: Raids from December 9 as Fire, once your gear has the crit for Ignite.
summary: Fire Blast and crits feed Heating Up for fast Pyroblasts, on top of 15% from Improved Scorch and 12% from Fire Power. It can out-damage Frost in short fights but runs out of mana first.
notes: Scorch until Improved Scorch has five stacks, Fire Blast on cooldown, Pyroblast whenever Heating Up has two or three stacks, Fireball otherwise. A three-second Pyroblast at two stacks already beats a Fireball.
Improved Fire Blast cuts Fire Blast’s cooldown to 6 seconds: a third more guaranteed Heating Up stacks. Incineration’s 10% crit turns more of them into two-stack Fire Blasts.
Fire Power reaches 12% with four of your Fire effects on the target: Improved Scorch, Fireball’s burn, Pyroblast’s burn and Ignite.

Master of Elements, Arcane Concentration and Missile Barrage’s free Missiles all stretch your mana, and Arcane Meditation keeps 17% of your mana regeneration going while you cast; plan Evocation and a mana gem into long fights. Arcane Blast gives 12% of your Intellect as spell damage for 18 seconds, so one Blast before a pull helps every Fire spell, and Arcane Subtlety lowers the target’s resistance to all your spells by 15. Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) take these same points; Burning Soul (30% less Fire threat) is the swap if you pull aggro.

name: Arcane
for: Raids from December 9 as Arcane: Arcane Blast and Arcane Power burst, the most mana spent.
summary: Arcane Blast stacks spell damage onto every spell for 18 seconds, Arcane Wrath and free Missile Barrage Missiles spend it, and Arcane Power adds 30% for 15 seconds. The biggest burst of the three and the hungriest for mana.
notes: Each Blast adds 12% of your Intellect as spell damage and makes the next Blast cost 100% more. Four in a row cost 150% of your base mana, and the fourth alone costs as much as the first and third together, so drop to two when mana runs low.

Inside those 18 seconds: Arcane Wrath on cooldown (3.3 seconds with two points of Accelerant, instant with Presence of Mind), Arcane Missiles on every Missile Barrage proc, which each Blast gives 40% of the time, and more Missiles to fill.
Arcane Subtlety cuts Arcane threat by 30% now that Blessing of Salvation is gone. Arcane Meditation keeps 50% of your mana regeneration going while you cast, and Mage Armor allows another 50%.

Arcane Mind doubles the crit bonus of Arcane spells, Incineration adds 10% crit to Arcane Blast, and Arcane Wrath also gains 5% of your maximum mana as spell damage. From Fire: Improved Fire Blast brings Fire Blast back every 6 seconds, each Fire Blast adds a Heating Up stack, and at three stacks Pyroblast casts in 1.5 seconds; Ignite adds 40% of every Fire crit as a burn. Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) take these same points.

name: Frost AoE
for: Big pulls in dungeons and AoE farming at 60, built around the slow.
summary: For big pulls in dungeons and AoE farming, built around the slow: Improved Blizzard and Permafrost slow a pack by 50% while it walks through your Blizzard, Frostbite freezes some of it, and Cone of Cold and Frost Nova win you the distance to cast again. Ice Barrier soaks hits from 40.
notes: Since November 13 Frost Nova breaks on Blizzard’s damage and on damage from procs, so a pack frozen by Frost Nova and then hit by Blizzard walks free. Gather the pack, Frost Nova to get out of melee, and start Blizzard where they will walk: Improved Blizzard slows them by 40%, 50% with Permafrost, and every tick renews it.

When they come out of the Blizzard, Cone of Cold slows them by 40%, the first four by 10% more for 3 sec longer; step back and start the next Blizzard. Arctic Reach adds 20% to Blizzard’s range and to the radius of Cone of Cold and Frost Nova, and each of Blizzard’s chills gives Frostbite a 15% chance to freeze a mob for 5 sec.
Use your top rank of Blizzard: a rank learned more than 12 levels below you still has a reduced chance to trigger Frostbite and Clearcasting.
Shatter and Ice Shards make Cone of Cold and Frost Nova crit more often and for double damage on a frozen pack. Cold Snap gives you a second Frost Nova and Ice Block when a pull goes wrong.

Frost Channeling’s 30% threat cut helps a tank keep the pack off you. The build is 11 points from the Frost PvE build: Winter’s Chill, Fingers of Frost, Missile Barrage and Magic Absorption trade for the control talents. Icy Veins’ AoE build (November 10) takes Fingers of Frost and eighteen Arcane points instead of Improved Frostbolt, Frostbite and Arctic Reach.

name: Frost
for: Battlegrounds and world PvP as Frost: control, Ice Block and Cold Snap.
summary: Ice Barrier every 30 seconds, Cold Snap for a second Ice Block or Frost Nova, and shatter combos from Frost Nova, Frostbite and Fingers of Frost.
notes: Shatter combo: Frost Nova or a Frostbite freeze, then Frostbolt and Ice Lance before it breaks. Fingers of Frost makes your next two spells count as frozen without a freeze, so it still works once roots have diminishing returns.
Ice Barrier with Frost Warding absorbs 983 damage plus 12% of your Frost spell power, adds about 20% Frost damage and stops pushback while it holds. Recast it whenever it breaks.
Winter’s Chill stacks on every Frostbolt, so Cone of Cold becomes an instant finisher when a melee player closes in: double damage at five stacks, and Shatter’s 50% crit on a frozen target.

Rank 1 Frostbolt is a one-second cast with Improved Frostbolt, slows by 50% with Permafrost and still procs Frostbite and Fingers of Frost. Two ranks of Precision cover the hit you need against players.
Cold Snap resets Ice Block, Frost Nova, Ice Barrier, Cone of Cold and Ice Lance: save it for a second Ice Block or Frost Nova.

name: Arcane
for: PvP burst with Presence of Mind and Arcane Power, and Frost’s roots.
summary: Burst from Arcane Power and Presence of Mind, a 4 second silence on Counterspell, and a Frost dip to Ice Block and Shatter, which makes Arcane crits on frozen targets far more likely.
notes: Burst: Arcane Power, then Presence of Mind into Arcane Wrath, then Arcane Blast and Missiles. Arcane Wrath also gains 5% of your maximum mana as spell damage.

Shatter adds 50% crit to every spell against a frozen target, Arcane included, and Arcane Mind makes Arcane crits deal double damage: Frost Nova or Frostbite into an instant Arcane Wrath and Ice Lance is the kill combo.
Improved Channeling stops damage from pushing back your Missiles and protects Blast and Wrath 70% of the time. Missiles check line of sight only when the channel starts.
Improved Counterspell adds a 4 second silence to Counterspell’s 10 second lockout. Arcane Geometry extends Polymorph, Counterspell and your Arcane spells to 36 yards.
There is no Ice Barrier or Cold Snap: Ice Block, Blink and Mana Shield, cheaper with Arcane Shielding, are your defense. Two ranks of Precision cover the hit you need against players.

name: Fire
for: PvP burst with Fire crits, Blast Wave and Frost’s control.
summary: Fire Blast and Heating Up for fast Pyroblasts, Impact stuns and Blast Wave, with Ice Block, Improved Frost Nova and Shatter from the Frost tree.
notes: Fire Blast, every 6 seconds and with a 35-yard range, adds a Heating Up stack each time, two on a crit. At three stacks Pyroblast is a 1.5 second cast.
Frost Nova, then Fire Blast and a fast Pyroblast: Shatter’s 50% crit works on Fire spells too, and every crit feeds Heating Up and Ignite.
Impact stuns on 10% of your Fire hits, Blast Wave dazes everything near you by 50% for 6 seconds, and Burning Soul stops 70% of pushback on your casts.
Frostfire Bolt is a 2.5 second cast with Accelerant that slows by 40% and counts as Fire and Frost: use it on runners and Fireball on casters.
Ice Block, Blink and Improved Frost Nova are your defense, and two ranks of Precision cover the hit you need against players.

name: Affliction
for: Solo questing with the Voidwalker tanking: the warlock’s default leveling build.
summary: Damage over time first: Corruption instant from 14, more mana from every Life Tap at 16, Pandemic and Malevolence for crits from 22, Siphon Life at 30, Soul Siphon by 33 and Wrack at 40, then your demon’s damage and health from Demonology. Drain Life and Siphon Life keep you healed between pulls.
notes: Improved Corruption (10 to 14) makes Corruption instant and 10% stronger, and Improved Life Tap (15 and 16) adds 20% to the mana of every Life Tap, which is where most of your mana comes from. Suppression (17 to 21) adds 5% hit. Pandemic (22 to 24) raises the crit damage bonus of Corruption, Bane of Agony, Siphon Life, your drains and Wrack by 100%, Improved Bane of Agony (25 and 26) adds 10% to Bane of Agony, and Malevolence (27 to 29, 34 and 41) adds 5% crit to Shadow spells.

Pull with Bane of Agony and Corruption, let the Voidwalker hold the mob and wand it down; since November 10 every demon has about 15% more base health. Siphon Life comes at 30, and Soul Siphon (31 to 33) adds 12% to Drain Life, Drain Soul and Wrack for each of Corruption, Siphon Life and Bane of Agony on the target, up to 36%.

Wrack (40) channels for 6 sec at 60 Shadow damage a second, and while you channel it your Corruption, Siphon Life and Bane of Agony tick twice as fast, so put the three on first, then channel Wrack. Since November 10 it deals 30% less, and the faster ticks replace its old 10% bonus to those three. Shadow Mastery (35 to 39) adds 10% to your Shadow damage, and Nightfall (42 and 43) gives the ticks of Corruption, your drains and Wrack a 4% chance at an instant Shadow Bolt. Icy Veins (November 4) spends 31 to 41 in Demonology for Demonic Sacrifice instead, for the Felhunter’s 3% of your Health every 4 sec, and reaches Wrack only at level 51; Wowhead (November 11) reaches it at level 47 without a respec, or at 40 with one, as here.

Finish a mob with Drain Soul when you need a Soul Shard: since 2 November it rarely gives one from damage alone, but always does on a kill. Improved Drains (44 to 46) adds 20% to Drain Life and Drain Soul.

From 47 the demon gets stronger: Unholy Power (47 to 51, 10% more demon damage), Demonic Energies (52 and 53: your spell damage heals the demon for 15%, and Life Tap fills its mana too) and Fel Vitality (54 to 56: 15% more health and mana for the demon, 15% more mana for you). Fel Concentration (57 to 59) and a point of Demonic Embrace finish it. Amplify Curse and Curse of Exhaustion are left out: one strengthens a single Bane of Agony every 3 min, the other only slows.

At 60 it is 13 points from the Affliction PvE build: Improved Drains, Fel Concentration, Unholy Power and Demonic Energies become four more points of Demonic Embrace, Demonic Aegis, Demonic Sacrifice, Amplify Curse and Improved Shadow Bolt.

name: Demonology
for: Warlocks who want the demon to do the work. Warcraft Tavern’s guide levels Affliction to 27 and respecs; this build is Demonology from 10.
summary: Your demon does more of the work: Demonic Brand (25-27) adds damage to its attacks, Soul Link (30) moves 30% of the damage you take onto it, and Demonic Pact (40) lets you keep a sacrifice and a demon. It is safe while the demon lives, which takes more care now that pets have less Health.
notes: Unholy Power (10-14), Fel Vitality (15-17) and Demonic Energies (18-19) first: 10% more demon damage, 15% more Health for the demon and 15% more mana for you, and the demon heals for 15% of the spell damage you deal.

Demonic Sacrifice (20) is the way to Soul Link. Pets gain only 2 Health per point of your Stamina since 2 November (since 10 November the demons have about 15% more base health), so Improved Health Funnel (23-24) moves 40% more health to the demon, Master Summoner (21-22) cuts a summon to 6 seconds and Fel Domination (28) to half a second once every 5 minutes.

Demonic Brand: cast Searing Pain and your demon’s next six attacks on that target deal extra Fire or Shadow damage. The Voidwalker’s Shadow brand carries high threat, so it also holds the mob for you.

From 40, sacrifice a Felhunter (3% of your Health every 4 sec for 2 hours) and then summon the Voidwalker: Demonic Pact keeps the buff, and Master Demonologist (35-39) cuts the Physical damage you both take by 10%. Improved Corruption (41-45) and Bane (46-50) come next. Icy Veins (November 4) and Wowhead (November 6) put the points after 40 into Affliction instead, with Pandemic and Improved Drains for Drain Life: that suits a warlock who drains a lot, and Bane here is the raid build’s Shadow Bolt.

At 60 the Demonology PvE build is 18 points away: Improved Shadow Bolt, Ruin, Agonizing Flames, Decimation and Improved Sayaad instead of Improved Corruption, Suppression, Improved Life Tap, Cataclysm, Fel Domination, Improved Health Funnel and Improved Voidwalker.

name: Destruction
for: Warlocks who level in dungeons and groups: Shadow Bolt and Conflagrate burst, more drinking solo.
summary: Destruction kills each mob fastest with Immolate, Conflagrate (25) and Shadowburn, but it spends the most mana and has no drains to heal you, so your Voidwalker has to hold threat while you nuke.
notes: Bane (10-14) speeds up Shadow Bolt and Immolate, and Cataclysm (15-17) cuts their mana cost. Cast Shadowburn (20) on a dying mob: if it dies within 8 seconds you get the Soul Shard back.
From 25: Immolate, Conflagrate, then Shadow Bolt. Ruin (21-24, 29) doubles the bonus damage of your crits and Fire and Brimstone (30-32) adds 25% crit to Conflagrate.

Shadow and Flame (35-39) stops Conflagrate from using up your Immolate and makes Shadowburn refund its Soul Shard, and each gives 20% to the other school for 20 seconds. Incinerate (40) is then your filler, 25% stronger on a target with your Immolate. Wowhead (November 6) calls this deep build its dungeon build; its solo build leaves Destruction after Conflagrate and puts the rest into Unholy Power and Affliction instead, for less drinking alone.

Since 2 November pets gain only 2 Health per point of your Stamina (since 10 November the demons have about 15% more base health), so let the Voidwalker build threat before you nuke. Molten Skin (41-45) cuts all damage you take by 10% and Intensity (46-48) keeps your casts on time when a mob reaches you.
At 60 the Destruction PvE build is 11 points away: Demonic Sacrifice and its ten Demonology points instead of Molten Skin, Intensity, Improved Life Tap and one rank of Improved Corruption.

name: Affliction
for: Raids from December 9 as Affliction: Wrack as the filler under three DoTs.
summary: The PvE spec to start with: Corruption, Bane of Agony and Siphon Life tick twice as fast while you channel Wrack, as Blizzard’s hotfixes of 10 November made it. It needs the least Life Tapping of the three and no demon to keep alive.
notes: Wrack is the filler, not Shadow Bolt: it deals 60 damage a second at 60 plus part of your spell power, and for its 6 seconds your Corruption, Bane of Agony and Siphon Life deal their damage twice as fast, so refresh them as they run out. With all three on the target Soul Siphon adds 36% to it, Pandemic doubles its crit bonus and each tick can trigger Nightfall.
Sacrifice the Imp with Demonic Sacrifice for 15% more Shadow damage for 2 hours: every spell you cast is Shadow. The other Demonology points add 15% Stamina, 15% mana and a stronger Demon Armor.

Suppression covers 5% hit and cuts your threat by 20%. Improved Bane of Agony and Amplify Curse make Bane of Agony the one to use; Bane of Doom is about as good on a boss that lives past a minute and costs fewer casts. Improved Shadow Bolt: a Shadow Bolt crit makes the target take 20% more Shadow damage from you for 12 sec, so spend every Nightfall on a Shadow Bolt. Icy Veins (November 4) and Wowhead (November 11) both take it, instead of Fel Concentration and Grim Reach; Icy Veins also skips Demonic Sacrifice for Ruin and Bane.

name: Destruction
for: Raids from December 9 as Destruction: Incinerate and Shadow Bolt with the most burst.
summary: Fire with a Shadow assist: Incinerate is the filler, Conflagrate and Shadowburn keep both of Shadow and Flame’s 20% bonuses up, and a sacrificed Succubus adds 15% to your Fire damage.
notes: Shadow and Flame’s bonuses last 20 seconds. At five ranks Conflagrate never uses up your Immolate, so cast it every 10 seconds, and one Shadowburn every 15 to 20 seconds keeps the Fire bonus up and refunds its Soul Shard.

Incinerate beats Shadow Bolt here: with Bane it casts in 2 seconds and deals 25% more to a target with your Immolate, about 25 to 30% more damage per second of casting. So the build skips Improved Shadow Bolt and takes Suppression for hit.

Destruction spends the most mana of the three, hence Cataclysm and Fel Vitality. Aftermath at five ranks adds 50% to Immolate’s first hit; Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) both take all five. On a two-target fight, Bane of Havoc on the second target copies 15% of your damage to it. Wowhead ranks this Demonic Sacrifice build behind keeping the Sayaad out, with Unholy Power and Affliction points instead of the sacrifice.

name: Demonology
for: Raid groups that want Demonic Pact and a strong demon.
summary: Sacrifice the Imp for 15% Shadow damage, then fight with the Succubus or Incubus: Demonic Pact keeps the sacrifice, while Master Demonologist, Soul Link and Demonic Knowledge add more for as long as the demon lives.
notes: Shadow Bolt is the filler, faster with Bane and stronger with Improved Shadow Bolt, Ruin and Agonizing Flames, which adds 10% to all your Destruction spells, Searing Pain and Soul Fire included. Two points of Suppression keep some hit and threat reduction. Every 10 seconds cast Searing Pain: Demonic Brand makes your demon’s next six attacks on the target deal extra Shadow damage, with high threat.

Everything but the sacrifice needs the demon alive, and it has less Health since 2 November, though about 15% more base health came back on 10 November. Demonic Energies heals it for 15% of your spell damage; if it dies, Master Summoner takes 4 seconds off the summon. Improved Sayaad adds 30% to Lash of Pain: Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) both take it, instead of Demonic Embrace and Fel Domination.
Decimation: below 35% health your Shadow Bolts deal 6% more, and Soul Fire casts 40% faster and costs no Soul Shard.

name: Destruction
for: PvP burst: Conflagrate, Shadowburn and Soul Fire.
summary: The most burst a warlock has: Immolate, then Conflagrate, Shadowburn and Death Coil within a few seconds, with Ruin doubling the bonus of every crit. The sacrificed Succubus’s 15% Fire damage is a buff, not a demon an enemy can kill.
notes: Open with Immolate, then Conflagrate (it keeps the Immolate and dazes the target), Shadowburn (it refunds its Soul Shard), Incinerate, and Death Coil to heal. Crits have dealt full damage in PvP since 8 October.

Molten Skin cuts all damage you take by 6% at three ranks and Intensity stops 70% of hits from pushing back your casts. Four ranks of Suppression give the 4% hit that stops your spells missing players of your level.

With no demon you have no Spell Lock or Seduction: control with Fear, Howl of Terror and Death Coil, and put Curse of Tongues on casters. Sacrifice the Felhunter instead (3% of your Health every 4 sec) when you need staying power more than burst.

name: Affliction
for: PvP pressure that wins long fights: DoTs, drains and Wrack.
summary: Pressure and staying power: your DoTs and Wrack wear the target down while Drain Life heals you, Curse of Exhaustion and Grim Reach’s extra range keep melee off you, and the Felhunter brings Spell Lock and Devour Magic.
notes: Corruption, Bane of Agony, Siphon Life and a curse, then Wrack, or Drain Life when you need health: Improved Drains, Soul Siphon and Shadow Mastery all raise its healing. Fel Concentration keeps both channels going through 70% of hits.

Since 2 November pets gain only 2 Health per point of your Stamina, softened by the 15% more base health Blizzard gave the demons on 10 November: Fel Vitality adds 15% to the Felhunter’s Health and Demonic Energies heals it for 15% of your spell damage. Soul Link is left out, because the 30% of your damage it moves onto the demon would kill it quickly.
Devour Magic can take a Polymorph or a Fear off you, and Spell Lock interrupts a heal and locks that school for 8 seconds.
Four ranks of Suppression give the 4% hit that stops Fear and your DoTs missing players of your level. The fifth only matters against higher levels.

name: Demonology
for: PvP with Soul Link and a demon that survives: the hardest warlock to kill.
summary: The defensive spec: a sacrificed demon’s buff and a living demon at once, with Soul Link moving 30% of the damage you take onto it and Master Demonologist cutting damage for both of you.
notes: Against casters, sacrifice the Imp (15% Shadow damage) and fight with the Felhunter: 10% less Magic damage for both of you, and Improved Felhunter cuts Spell Lock’s cooldown to 24 seconds. Against melee, sacrifice the Felhunter (3% of your Health every 4 sec) and fight with the Voidwalker for 10% less Physical damage.

Your demon is the weak point: it has less Health since 2 November, even with the 15% more base health of 10 November, and Soul Link feeds it 30% of your damage. Demonic Energies heals it, Improved Health Funnel heals it faster, and Master Summoner with Fel Domination bring it back in half a second.

Demonic Brand adds burst through the demon after each Searing Pain. The Affliction points bring instant Corruption, Curse of Exhaustion, stronger Drain Life and four ranks of Suppression, the 4% hit that stops your spells missing players of your level.

name: Feral
for: Solo questing for any druid: a cat that spends no mana in a fight and heals itself between pulls.
summary: Level as a cat, with Bear Form until 20: you spend no mana while you fight and heal yourself quickly between pulls. Shifting Power arrives at 40, and Heart of the Wild and Naturalist add 10% Strength and 10% damage by 50.
notes: Levels 10-19 in Bear Form: Ferocity (10-14) makes Maul cost 10 Rage and Swipe 15, Feral Swiftness (15-16) adds 4% dodge in every form and, from 20, 30% run speed in Cat Form, and Furor (17-19) gives a 60% chance of 10 Rage each time you shift into Bear Form.

Cat Form at 20: Feral Charge (20) leaps you behind the mob for a Shred opener, then Claw is your builder, Rake and Rip keep it bleeding and Ferocious Bite (new first rank at 24) finishes. Savage Fury (21-22), Sharpened Claws (23-24), Predatory Strikes (25-27) and Blood Frenzy (28-29) lead to Leader of the Pack at 30; from 32 you open with Prowl and Ravage, 10 Energy cheaper with Poised.

Rend and Tear (35-39) adds 15% to your melee abilities against a bleeding target: Rake and Rip, and since November 11 Pounce’s bleed too, and Shifting Power comes at 40 (it needs Predatory Discipline, taken at 33): 40 Energy for mana a cat does not otherwise spend. Heart of the Wild (41-45) and Naturalist (46-50) follow, and Furor’s fourth and fifth points (34 and 51) give back all your Energy when you return to Cat Form after a heal.

Then Furor’s last point (51) and Balance: Genesis (52-56) adds 10% to the periodic damage of Rake, Rip and Pounce, Nature’s Majesty (57-58) adds 4% crit to your melee attacks, and two points of Natural Shapeshifter (59-60) make shifting 20% cheaper. Icy Veins and Wowhead end on the same Genesis and Nature’s Majesty points; they also take Lacerate and Primal Bite, for a druid who tanks in Bear Form, which a cat does not need. At 60 the build is 4 points from the Feral cat build: Feral Swiftness and Nature’s Majesty become Shredding Attacks and the third point of Natural Shapeshifter.

name: Restoration
for: Druids who will heal: you kill as a bear and a cat with Restoration’s form talents and heal dungeons by your late 20s.
summary: You still kill as a bear and a cat: Heart of the Wild and Naturalist work in forms. The healing talents come along the way, Wild Growth at 40 for dungeons, and the build ends on the Restoration PvE build.
notes: Heart of the Wild (10-14) adds 20% Stamina in Bear Form, 10% Strength in Cat Form and 10% Intellect, and Naturalist (15-19) adds 10% to all your damage, so bear and cat kill well enough without Feral talents and your mana goes to heals. Icy Veins (November 4) levels as a Wrath caster in Balance to 33 instead and reaches Wild Growth only at level 58, a path for questing alone. Wowhead (November 13) has the same two paths: a Balance and Restoration build for questing, and a healing build with Wild Growth for dungeons, close to this one.

Reflection (20-22), Gift of Nature (23-24 and 26-28), Swiftmend (25), Bloom (29) and Nature’s Swiftness (30) make you a dungeon healer by your late 20s. If you mostly heal dungeons, swap the two: Nature’s Focus first and Heart of the Wild last; nothing else moves.
Living Spirit (31-33), Improved Rejuvenation (34-36) and Improved Regrowth (37-39) are the price of Wild Growth at 40. Genesis (43-47) then adds 10% to every heal over time, and to Rake and Rip.

Since November 13 Wild Growth can no longer be cast on the move and gains twice as much from your healing power (6.6%, was 3.3%). The client read by foreverchanges.pro the same day also has its three ranks sharing one cooldown, which Blizzard has not posted. At 60 it matches the Restoration PvE build point for point, so there is nothing to respec.

name: Balance
for: Druids who prefer casting: Moonfire and Starfire from range, more drinking than a cat.
summary: Slower than Feral: you cast from range and rest more between pulls. Improved Wrath makes Wrath cheap enough to spam, Improved Starfire adds a stun chance and Moonkin Form comes at 40.
notes: Improved Wrath first (10-14): half a second faster and half the mana. Moonglow (15-17) takes 25% off every damaging spell and Nature’s Reach (18-19) adds 20% range and 4% hit, so you land more casts before the mob reaches you. Entangling Roots and Bear Form are your escapes. Icy Veins (November 4) puts 15 to 22 into Nature’s Focus and Reflection instead and reaches Moonkin Form only at level 53, for less drinking before 40. Wowhead’s recommended build (November 4) takes Improved Wrath, Moonglow and Nature’s Reach first as here, Moonkin Form from 40, and ends on the same 51 points.

Nature’s Majesty (20-21) adds 4% crit and opens Nature’s Splendor (22), which with Improved Moonfire (23-24) makes Moonfire a better opener; Insect Swarm comes at 25, and Improved Starfire (26-30) gives Starfire a 15% chance to stun for 3 sec.

Eclipse (32-34): each Wrath takes 0.5 sec off your next two Starfires. Moonfury (35-39), Moonkin Form at 40 (360% more armor from items), then Vengeance (41-45), which makes Arcane and Nature crits deal double damage.
Nature’s Focus (46-50) stops 70% of hits from pushing back your casts; take it before Vengeance if mobs keep reaching you. Naturalist (51-55) and Reflection (56-58) follow.
At 60 it is 5 points from the Balance PvE build (Nature’s Focus instead of Heart of the Wild): respec only if you raid.

name: Restoration
for: Raid and dungeon healers from December 9: Wild Growth, Swiftmend and Bloom.
summary: Wild Growth heals a whole party, Swiftmend heals for the full duration of the heal over time it consumes, and Bloom heals for 100% of your Spirit whenever a Rejuvenation or Regrowth runs out.
notes: Nature’s Splendor stretches Rejuvenation to 15 sec and Regrowth to 27 for the same mana, and Swiftmend then consumes 15 sec of Rejuvenation. Reaching it costs ten Balance points: Genesis (10% to every heal over time) and Nature’s Majesty (4% crit) earn theirs, Moonglow is the price.

Heart of the Wild and Nature’s Focus both: 10% Intellect for mana, and 70% of hits no longer push back your casts. Tranquil Spirit is skipped, because Healing Touch, the main spell it discounts, is your least efficient heal. Icy Veins’ build and Wowhead’s Deep Resto build (November 4) take Improved Wrath, Nature’s Reach and Insect Swarm for damage between heals instead of Nature’s Focus and Improved Tranquility; Wowhead recommends a Nature’s Grace and Improved Regrowth build for raids, written before Wild Growth changed on November 13.

Improved Tranquility makes Tranquility a 2 min cooldown with no threat, and since Blizzard’s hotfixes of 10 November Nature’s Swiftness makes a Wild Growth instant too. Swiftmend only consumes your own Rejuvenation or Regrowth.

Since November 13 Wild Growth can no longer be cast on the move and gains twice as much from your healing power (6.6%, was 3.3%). The client read by foreverchanges.pro the same day also has its three ranks sharing one cooldown, which Blizzard has not posted.

name: Feral bear
for: Druid tanks for dungeons and raids: Lacerate, Primal Bite and Swipe.
summary: Bear Form and Dire Bear Form add 115% threat, and Lacerate and Primal Bite add more. Feral Swiftness and Natural Reaction add 9% dodge, Thick Hide armor and Heart of the Wild 20% Stamina in Bear Form.
notes: Lacerate stacks a high-threat bleed up to five times and keeps Rend and Tear’s 15% on Maul, Swipe and Primal Bite. Primal Bite (6 sec cooldown) sits in the last row behind Leader of the Pack.

Rage: critical strikes in Bear Form give 100% more Rage, Blood Frenzy adds 5 per crit and Natural Reaction 5 per dodge. Natural Instinct adds 20% to your crit bonus and three points of Genesis 6% to Lacerate’s bleed. Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) take Natural Instinct and nine Balance points instead of Natural Reaction and Furor; Natural Reaction stays here for its 5% dodge, and Furor’s 10 Rage on entering Bear Form goes.

Thick Hide adds 180 base armor at 60, plus 2 for every point of Defense above 300, and Dire Bear Form multiplies it. Feral Instinct makes Swipe hit 30% harder on packs; if you only tank bosses, Shredding Attacks (Lacerate 3 Rage cheaper) is the swap.

name: Feral cat
for: Raids from December 9 as a cat: Shred, Rake and Rip with Shifting Power.
summary: Shred, Rake and Rip, with Rend and Tear adding 15% against bleeding targets. Shifting Power turns mana into 40 Energy every 8 sec, so mana is Energy, and Natural Shapeshifter makes each one 30% cheaper.
notes: Shifting Power needs Predatory Discipline, which also lets Ferocious Bite keep your spare Energy: it still adds damage for the Energy above its cost but no longer spends it, so bite at high Energy.

Natural Shapeshifter gets you about 43% more Shifting Powers from the same mana, and mana potions now work in Cat Form. Genesis adds 10% to Rake, Rip and Pounce ticks; Naturalist adds 10% to everything. Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) take Feral Swiftness and Nature’s Majesty instead of Natural Shapeshifter and Furor’s last two points: 4% crit against fewer Shifting Powers.
Furor keeps your Energy when you shift out to Innervate, resurrect or heal. Feral Charge leaps you behind the target after the boss moves.

name: Balance
for: Raids from December 9 as Balance: Eclipse between Wrath and Starfire.
summary: Eclipse ties the two nukes together: each Wrath takes half a second off your next two Starfires. Improved Wrath, Moonglow and Reflection decide how long you can keep the Starfires going.
notes: With Improved Wrath and Improved Starfire, a 1.5 sec Wrath takes 1 sec off the next two Starfires (3 sec down to 2.5), so it costs half a second of casting and adds its own damage.

Heart of the Wild instead of Nature’s Focus: you are rarely hit in a raid, and 10% Intellect is more mana. Naturalist adds 10% to all damage, Nature’s Reach 4% hit. Icy Veins and Wowhead (November 4) keep Nature’s Focus instead; Icy Veins names Heart of the Wild as the swap when nothing delays your casts.
Moonkin Form still doubles Omen of Clarity’s chance to proc, but its 3% crit does not stack with Leader of the Pack.

name: Feral
for: PvP as a cat: stun openers from Prowl and burst from Shred.
summary: Cat burst with bear control: Brutal Impact makes Bash a 5 sec stun every 30 sec, Furor gives you the 10 Rage it costs as you enter Bear Form, and both capstones fit.
notes: Shifting out of Cat Form breaks roots and snares, and Furor brings back the Energy you left with; Natural Shapeshifter makes every shift 30% cheaper. Mana is what runs out, so spend it on shifts and Shifting Power.

Open from Prowl with Pounce (a 3 sec stun with Brutal Impact, and since November 11 its bleed counts for Rend and Tear) or Ravage, Shred while they are stunned and Claw when they face you. Predatory Discipline lets a Ferocious Bite at high Energy keep the spare Energy.
Primal Bite is the spare point: a real attack when you turn bear to survive. To carry flags, move Rend and Tear’s five points to Natural Reaction for 5% dodge.

name: Restoration
for: PvP healers who shift out of roots: Nature’s Swiftness, Swiftmend and Wild Growth.
summary: Heals that work on the move: Rejuvenation and Swiftmend are instant, Nature’s Swiftness makes a Healing Touch instant, and Furor gives you the 10 Rage for a Bash when you shift into Bear Form, which Brutal Impact makes a 5 sec stun every 30 sec.
notes: Natural Shapeshifter makes Bear, Cat and Travel Form 30% cheaper, so you can shift out of every root and snare, and Heart of the Wild adds 20% Stamina in Bear Form.
Nature’s Focus keeps 70% of hits from pushing back Regrowth and Healing Touch. Bloom heals for 50% of your Spirit when an enemy dispels your Rejuvenation or Regrowth.
Genesis (10% to every heal over time) and Nature’s Majesty (4% crit) are the Balance points; one point of Improved Regrowth is enough here, and the two it saves go to Brutal Impact.

Since November 13 Wild Growth can no longer be cast on the move and gains twice as much from your healing power (6.6%, was 3.3%). The client read by foreverchanges.pro the same day also has its three ranks sharing one cooldown, which Blizzard has not posted.

name: Balance
for: PvP casters: Starfire burst and roots from range.
summary: Moonkin Form multiplies your item armor and blocks Polymorph, Entangling Roots hold up to three targets, and Starfire has a 15% chance to stun.
notes: Improved Entangling Roots lets a rooted target take 75% more damage before breaking free, Overgrowth keeps up to three roots at once, and Nature’s Reach’s 20% range keeps you out of melee.
Nature’s Focus stops 70% of hits from pushing back your casts. Moonkin Form blocks healing spells: shift out to heal, which also clears roots and snares.
No Genesis or Reflection: fights are short, and the points go to control.
